modules.doc: Amoeba Phase 1 — Task → Plan a new team → Team runs the task.
`python -m amoeba ...` is the `amoeba` command (amoeba/cli.py).
Phase 2: the adaptation loop (Boxes 4–9; spec/BUILD_SPEC_PHASE2.md). Only the Architect (Box 6) calls a model;
D83 — Box 7, the Experimenter (Phase 2 spec §8). Plain code; it calls no model itself — it runs Boxes 1–3 (which
D81 — the team recipe, the edit menu and validation (Phase 2 spec §3).
D80 — Box 0, the task stream (Phase 2 spec §2).
Capability names (D29): map what models call a tool or skill onto one canonical name, from aliases.yaml.
The `amoeba` command (also `python -m amoeba`).
YAML persistence and a content hash for TeamConfig.
Prompt files copied verbatim from the source repos (spec §7), one source-header line each.
Team configuration schema (spec §4). Names match the full BUILD_SPEC so later phases add fields, not renames.
Static validation of a TeamConfig against the envelope (spec §4.1). Returns a list of errors; empty = valid.
D74 — citation check by code: what a step cites a source for must be in that source.
D75 — the run's clock: today's date, weekday and time zone, given to every Box 3 step prompt.
D67 — freshness of figures for tasks that ask for today's, the current or the latest value.
BOX 3 — the `plan` topology (D31): carry out a d24 plan over its depends_on graph.
D33 — provenance: every number a step writes must be traceable, and plain code counts which ones are not.
BOX 3 — Team runs the task (spec §6). Two explicit topology runners; plain code owns loops, caps, parsing, trace.
D64 — shorten a text for a later reader without cutting away its result.
TraceWriter — one JSONL line per span, OpenTelemetry GenAI attribute names — and the traced LLM wrapper.
D46 — a response cache for LLM replies and web tool results, so a run can be recorded once and replayed free.
LLM clients — pattern from jiuwen_atm/llm_client.py (MIT): one OpenAI-compatible client, one mock.
D47 — opt-in per-run limits and the cost estimate.
D54 — named model profiles (amoeba/config/models.yaml) and per-role routing.
A scripted stand-in for a model on the toy tasks, so `scripts/run_task.py --toy` runs offline.
D59 — the local toolbox: Claude Code's tools and skills through `claude mcp serve`, sandboxed (--local-tools on).
D59 — a step that says it made a file must have made it (plain code, with --local-tools on only).
D59 — the plain-code gate in front of every local tool call. It never asks a model.
D71 — the office suite in the sandbox: LibreOffice headless, so spreadsheet formulas get computed values.
D59 — one `claude mcp serve` process per run, over stdio, with the official MCP Python SDK.
D59 — local skills: Claude Code's skill folders and the anthropics/skills clone kept by `pool refresh`.
D59 — the local toolbox: Claude Code's Bash, Read, Write, Edit (and Glob, Grep when the server offers them) as
The Memory box (first stub, D77): what the system knows about the user, read-only.
D77 — the user context file (--context user.yaml): who is asking, so the task can be read the way they mean it.
D56 — the tool/skill pool Box 3 stocks its toolbox from: index (refresh, cache), match, stock (pick, vet,
D56 — the pool index: every tool and skill Box 3 may stock its toolbox from, cached on disk (0 tokens).
D56 — match a capability request to pool entries by keyword overlap (plain code, 0 tokens, no embeddings).
D56 — pool tools: remote MCP servers called through ToolRegistry.execute, with the limits of web_search.
D56 — Box 3 starts by stocking the toolbox: each capability request Box 2 recorded may be filled from the pool.
The envelope: tool allowlists per role and the roster cap. No cost fields in Phase 1 (spec §2 "Cost").
BOX 2 — Plan a new team: the AutoAgents drafting trio (spec §5.2), then deterministic post-checks.
Deterministic scoring for toy tasks. No AI judge in Phase 1 (that is Phase 2, as a signal only).
Draft → TeamConfig (spec §5.3). Plain code: durable ids, edges, entry/exit, validation.
D77 — task understanding before planning (Box 1 → Box 2).
Data records passed between the three boxes.
Deterministic parsers — regexes copied from the source code (spec §5.1). Departures are marked DEVIATION.
Deterministic checks on a finished draft (D24, spec/BOX2_PROMPT_UPGRADE_D24.md §4.4).
D45 — reuse saved Box 2 drafts instead of drafting again.
Toy tasks with known answers — the same ones every time for a given seed. Three families in Phase 1.
Tool registry with `echo` and `calc`. Dispatch by name (AutoAgents routes every drafted tool to SerpAPI — D7).
D32 — the first real tools: web_search and fetch_url, behind one provider interface (Tavily for now).
A readable Markdown transcript of Box 2 attempts from an eval_draft output folder (drafts/<task>.<n>.json).
Box 2 only: draft a team for each task, several times, and measure the drafting step. No helper runs.
Copy the prompt templates verbatim out of the source clones into amoeba/config/prompts/.
D54: print the models an OpenAI-compatible endpoint offers, to check a profile's model names before a run.
Phase 2 week-1 check (spec §8): one hand-written hypothesis through Box 7 (the Experimenter) — and, from D84, Box 8.
CLI (spec §10): draft a team for a task, run it, write runs/<run_id>/{team.yaml, plan.json, trace.jsonl,

prompts.header: # source: ours — DEVIATION D24, spec/BOX2_PROMPT_UPGRADE_D24.md §3.2 (Planner prompt)
prompts.text:
# Task
${context}

# Existing expert roles (reuse if they fit)
${existing_roles}

# Tools the team will have when it runs (use them where they fit; do NOT let this list limit the plan)
${tools}${lessons}

# History (your previous draft)
${history}

# Reviewer suggestions (latest round)
${suggestions}

# How to plan
Work in this order and write each section.

1. Requirements. List every deliverable and requirement stated or clearly implied by the task, one per
   line with an id (R1, R2, ...). Keep the task's own verbs: "gather current", "prototype and test",
   "estimate", "deliver". Never weaken a requirement (e.g. "test" must stay "test", not "estimate").
2. Givens and derived numbers. List the numbers in the task and anything that follows from them
   (show the arithmetic). List assumptions you must make, each marked as an assumption.
   Open questions (optional): where the task is ambiguous and you settled it by an assumption, write
   each under "## Open Questions", one per line as "- question: ... | assumption: ...". Write None if
   nothing in the task was ambiguous. What the task's names and terms mean (which organisation, place, product
   or person it is about) is not yours to settle: when the task carries a "Working interpretation", plan on it
   exactly and do not guess another reading; if it is still unclear what the task is about, write the question
   with "assumption: not settled" rather than guessing.
3. Ideal capabilities. Before choosing roles, decide what abilities the work needs, as if any reasonable
   tool or skill were available. A TOOL is something that acts or fetches (web search, code execution,
   a database sandbox, a file reader). A SKILL is know-how or a method (cost modelling, schema design,
   GDPR transfer analysis, risk assessment). A document format (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf) or a house style is a
   SKILL, not a tool.
4. Roles. Create the smallest team of well-defined specialists (at most ${max_agents} including the
   final writer) that covers every requirement. A role is well defined only if it has ALL of these fields:
   {
     "name": "Cloud Cost Analyst",
     "seniority": "senior",
     "description": "who they are and why they are on this team (2-3 sentences)",
     "goal": "the single outcome this role is accountable for",
     "responsibilities": ["...", "..."],
     "skills": ["managed-database pricing models", "TCO modelling", "..."],
     "tools": ["the tools this role ideally needs, installed or not"],
     "inputs": ["what it receives and from which step"],
     "outputs": [{"artifact": "cost table", "format": "markdown table: provider x db x monthly USD"}],
     "success_criteria": ["how we know the output is good enough"],
     "constraints": ["limits from the task, e.g. 12-person team, EU residency"],
     "covers": ["R2", "R3"],
     "is_summariser": false,
     "prompt": "the full working prompt for this specialist: persona, method step by step, what to check, and the exact output format. Write it as a senior practitioner would brief a peer."
   }
   Do not give a role a tool only to fill the field; an empty list is fine. Specialists produce the
   content (analysis, tables, plans); exactly one role has "is_summariser": true and only assembles and
   edits their outputs into the final deliverable — it creates no new analysis and has no tools.
5. Capability requests. For every tool or skill in step 3 that is not installed, add one request as a JSON
   blob with keys: name, kind (tool|skill), for_role, what_it_does, input, output, example_input,
   example_output. Requesting is expected and costs nothing now; hiding a need is a planning error.
6. Execution plan. Numbered steps. Each step's FIRST line must be "N. [Role A, Role B]: short title".
   Under it, indented lines:
     kind: work or verify — verify only when the step checks the numbers, sources or results of the steps it
           depends on (and is done by a role that did not produce them); everything else is work
     covers: R ids
     depends_on: step numbers (or none) — steps with no dependency between them may run in parallel
     do: what exactly happens, as sub-steps
     output: the artifact, starting with one or more format markers that plain code will check —

# source: ours (D63) — Box 3 Action Observer, one mid-run re-plan call (after AutoAgents NextAction, autoagents/actions/steps.py:16-53)
prompts.text:
You are the Action Observer of a team that is carrying out a plan. Plain code paused the run after a wave of steps because something went wrong or changed. Decide whether the rest of the plan should change.

# Task
${task}

${today}

# Requirements
${requirements}

# Why you are called (found by plain code)
${triggers}

# The plan now
${plan}

# What the finished steps produced
${outputs}

# What is blocked and why
${blocked}

# Tools and skills the team really has now
${tools}

# Roles on the team
${roles}

# What is left for re-planning
${left}

# Rules
- Keep finished work. A step that has run (done, partial or incomplete) cannot be changed, re-run or dropped. Change only steps that have not run.
- Prefer a path that uses the tools the team actually has. When a capability is missing (for example a weather or routing service), plan the step around what exists — web search for published figures, calc for arithmetic, local tools for code and files — instead of waiting for it.
- When a requirement cannot be met exactly, a clearly labelled estimate from the available tools is better than nothing. Never plan an unlabelled guess.
- A new capability request is only a request: plain code tries to fill it from the pool and the local tools. A step that depends on it must say what to do if it stays unfilled.
- If nothing needs to change, answer CONTINUE.

# Decisions (choose exactly one)
- CONTINUE: the plan stays as it is.
- REVISE_REMAINING: rewrite the steps that have not run. Under ## Steps write all of them in the Execution Plan format below: keep the number of a step you keep, number a new step from ${next} on. A not-run step you leave out is dropped.
- ADD_STEP: add one step. Under ## Steps write it with number ${next}; its depends_on may name only finished steps. You may add a line "feeds: <step numbers>" naming not-run steps that must wait for it.
- REASSIGN_STEP: give one not-run step to another role on the team. Under ## Steps write "step: <number>" and "role: <role name>".
- DROP_STEP: drop one not-run step. Under ## Steps write "step: <number>"; under ## Unmet write each requirement id it leaves unmet and why.
- ADD_ROLE: add one new role (at most once per run) and its step(s). Under ## Role write one role JSON blob with the keys name, goal, description, skills, tools, outputs, success_criteria, prompt; under ## Steps its step(s) in the Execution Plan format, numbered from ${next}.

Execution Plan format:
${next}. [Role Name]: title
   kind: work
   covers: R1
   depends_on: 1, 2
   do: what to do, with which tool
   output: what it hands on
   done_when: when it is finished

# Format
Your reply MUST use exactly these sections:

## Thought
your reasoning in 2-5 sentences

## Decision
one of CONTINUE, REVISE_REMAINING, ADD_STEP, REASSIGN_STEP, DROP_STEP, ADD_ROLE

## Reason
one or two sentences

## Steps
as the decision asks, or None

## Role
one role JSON blob for ADD_ROLE, or None

## Unmet
for DROP_STEP, or None

## Capability Requests
one JSON blob per request with the keys name, kind (tool|skill), for_role, what_it_does, input, output; or None

# Task
${task}

${today}

# Your role card
${card}

# Your step (step ${number})
${step}

# Inputs: outputs of the steps this step depends on
${inputs}

# Work done so far in this step
${completed}

# Facts and sources
- Tag every number, price, date, law or benchmark figure you write: [S#] when it comes from a tool result (use that result's id, including ids already in your inputs), or [unverified] when it comes from your own knowledge. Never write such a figure without a tag, and never cite an [S#] you have not seen.
- A number you compute from tagged inputs needs no tag if you show the calculation (for example 50 x 200 GB = 10,000 GB) or use calc. A result calc or a local tool gave you in this step is derived: never tag it [unverified].
- A number given in the task needs no tag; never tag it with a web source [S#].
- Keep the [S#] tags of any input you reuse.
- Prefer the source about the specific thing the task asks about (this branch, this product, this person) over general pages. Never infer a specific fact from a general page: an office list, a chain-wide schedule or a category page does not tell you what one location or one item does.

what you need to do now and how

## CurrentStep
the part of the step you are doing in this turn

one of ${tools}

## ActionInput
the input to the action

spec_table.ours: the prompts (as `*_d19` variants built at load time from the verbatim files, `CAPABILITY_EDITS`) say *prefer* existing tools and list a missing tool or skill under an optional `## Capability Requests` section as JSON `{name, kind: tool\|skill, for_role, what_it_does, input, output, example_input, example_output}`; observers see the requests and judge them on need only: a role using an unlisted tool gets "ADD a Capability Request", never "remove the tool", and a request is not to be dropped only because an existing tool could work around it. The source's `Select existing expert roles (from {tools})` slip is corrected to `{existing_roles}`. The draft records `requests_proposed` (distinct names asked for in round 1) and `requests_dropped_by_observers` (of those, absent from the final draft), also in `result.json`. An unregistered tool in a role's `tools` becomes `missing_tools` + a recorded request. All go to `runs/<id>/capability_requests.json` and one `capability_request` trace event each
spec_table.why: a planner forbidden to name what it lacks hides the gap; recording it is the input a later phase needs to fetch or build tools (not done in Phase 1)

spec_table.original: D5 as first built: the summariser is "the first role with no tools"; if none, code appends a Language Expert
spec_table.ours: `is_summariser` flag on the drafted role / `AgentSpec`: the role the planner marks `"is_summariser": true`, else the last role of the last plan step (= the flat exit). Nothing is appended; `language_expert.txt` removed
spec_table.why: having no tools says nothing about who writes the answer; a tool-using last step was wrongly given a stranger as boss

spec_table.original: AutoAgents echoes any non-tool action (custom_action.py:213)
spec_table.ours: a helper with `missing_tools` gets one line per tool in `{suggestions}`: "Tool X is unavailable this run; proceed without it or answer BLOCKED: X". An action or input starting `BLOCKED` ends that helper's step, is recorded in `blocked_steps` and a `blocked` event; a blocked last step without a Final Output gives `error="blocked"`. An action naming a tool the helper lacks → `unknown_tool` event and a notice instead of the echo; if unregistered, a `runtime_unknown_tool` request. Print and Final Output still echo
spec_table.why: a silent echo hides a missing capability; boss_reviewers ignores tools, as before

spec_table.original: AutoAgents parses role blobs with the non-greedy regex `{[\s\S]*?}` (environment.py:62)
spec_table.ours: brace-balanced JSON scan (`parse_json_objects`) on both d19 and d24; the regex stays as `parse_role_blobs` so T3 still checks it
spec_table.why: a `{placeholder}` in a role prompt or a nested object cut the blob at the first `}`: 17/40 real drafts failed (docs/real_runs/2026-09-23_gemini-3.1-flash-lite.md)

spec_table.original: `parse_blocks` keeps everything after a heading (common.py:31-59)
spec_table.ours: a bare `---` block is not a section, and a closing `---` line is dropped from a section body
spec_table.why: models copy the FORMAT_EXAMPLE's `---` fences; the closing one ended up in the answer (`"EPOLEVNE\n---"`), 11/11 flat answers scored 0

spec_table.original: Box 2 prompts are AutoAgents' (with the D19 edits): one "Manager Ethan" system message, "prefer existing tools", a concise one-line-per-step plan, five-key role blobs, "No Suggestions" consensus
spec_table.ours: `--draft-prompts d24` (default stays d19): our prompts (`config/prompts/d24_*.txt`, `${}` Template syntax) with a system message per role; the Planner writes Requirements (R ids), Givens and Assumptions (with arithmetic), full role records (goal, skills, inputs, outputs, success_criteria, constraints, covers, prompt), a plan with `covers / depends_on / do / output / done_when` per step, Capability Requests and Risks and Decisions, planning the ideal before mapping to installed tools; observers check against a list and end with `## Verdict APPROVE|REVISE` — consensus = both exactly APPROVE (a verdict still missing after one repair counts as REVISE). The fields are kept (`DraftedRole`, `DraftPlanStep`, `Draft.requirements/givens/risks`, `parse_plan_d24`), checked by `draft_quality` (recorded in plan.json, result.json and the trace, never used to reject), and reach Box 3 (a role card in `{role}`, the step detail in `{context}`, the card in critics' `${role_description}`). Planner calls ask for 8192 tokens, observers 2048; a reply with `finish_reason == "length"` is flagged (`truncated` event)
spec_table.why: the db-choice transcript: plans bent to the installed tools, no capability requests, thin roles, one-line steps, wrong arithmetic, no convergence (spec/BOX2_PROMPT_UPGRADE_D24.md)

spec_table.original: Consensus when both Suggestions contain the substring "No Suggestions" (manager.py:47, with D2)
spec_table.ours: d19: a reply that also lists any numbered suggestion is not an approval ("1. No Suggestions" still is)
spec_table.why: 3 of 9 real observer replies listed fixes and then said "No Suggestions."

spec_table.original: `parse_blocks` keeps only the first fenced block of a section (common.py:53)
spec_table.ours: `parse_sections(..., all_fences=True)` joins every fenced block of a section in order; drafting reads Planner replies this way (d19 and d24)
spec_table.why: gemini-3.5-flash wrote each role in its own ```` ```json ```` block, so roles 2..n were lost and 2/9 d19 drafts failed "roster size 1" (docs/real_runs/2026-09-23_d19_vs_d24.md)

spec_table.original: (ours) D24 gave observers 2048 tokens per reply
spec_table.ours: every drafting role defaults to 8192, set per role with `--planner-max-tokens` / `--observer-max-tokens` or `AMOEBA_MAX_TOKENS_PLANNER` / `_OBSERVER` / `_AGENT_OBSERVER` / `_PLAN_OBSERVER` (CLI > role env > observer env > default). A reply with `finish_reason == "length"` is retried once with double `max_tokens` and the second reply is accepted; both calls are traced (`truncated` events, `amoeba.retry_of_truncated`). Hidden reasoning tokens are recorded per call (`amoeba.usage.reasoning_tokens`: the API's `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, else `total_tokens − prompt − completion`), kept apart from `total_tokens`
spec_table.why: 17 gemini-3.5-flash d19 observer replies stopped at 2048 while showing < 600 output tokens: the hidden reasoning counts against the limit (a max_tokens=40 call returned empty text with 48 total tokens)

spec_table.original: (ours) D24 observers were told only "a different role checks numbers, sources or test results"; draft_quality's verification check was a proxy and nothing acted on it
spec_table.ours: the d24 Plan Observer must answer REVISE when no step verifies numbers, sources or test results by a role that did not produce them. `draft_quality` adds `independent_verification`: a step whose text/do/done_when says it verifies (check, review, validate, reconcile, audit …), depends on the producing steps, and shares no role with their producers (the summariser's own step does not count). Hard checks: `requirements_covered`, `independent_verification`, `summariser` (d19 is judged on tools and last-step ownership, since its prompt never asks for a declaration). `--quality-gate` (default off): after each round, a failed hard check blocks consensus and is sent to the Planner as a "## Quality Gate" suggestion list, within MAX_ROUNDS; the last draft is still published. Gate hits are recorded per round (`DraftRound.gate_failed`, `Draft.gate_hits`, a `quality_gate` trace event)
spec_table.why: only 1/9 and 3/9 d24 drafts had a verification step by a non-producer, yet both observers approved (docs/real_runs/2026-09-23_d19_vs_d24.md)

spec_table.original: (ours) capability requests were recorded under whatever name the model wrote
spec_table.ours: each `CapabilityRequest` also carries `canonical` and `mapped`: `normalise()` (amoeba/capabilities) = lowercase snake_case key, looked up in `amoeba/capabilities/aliases.yaml` (canonical → aliases; starts with web_search, code_execution, database_sandbox, pricing_api, spreadsheet, load_testing, trade_database). An unknown name is kept as written and listed as unmapped (`result.json.unmapped_capabilities`, the CLI's last lines, eval_draft's `unmapped_names`) so the file can be extended. `name` keeps the raw name in capability_requests.json; request survival and `tools_accounted` compare canonical names
spec_table.why: 67 distinct names in the first real runs, e.g. "Web Search", "web_search", "Web Research", "Market Research Tool" for one capability

spec_table.original: (ours) Phase 1 scored only tasks with a ground_truth; D24's derived-number check matched listed spellings ("21.9 TB") and missed the same bytes written in binary units
spec_table.ours: `Task.rubric` (optional; replaces `Task.expected`): required_deliverables and constraints_to_respect (regex any_of), expected_numbers (value + unit + tolerance, default 5%; a decimal byte unit also matches its binary reading, money accepts $/USD/million/M), must_not (a pattern that fails unless `unless_nearby`, e.g. a source, is within `window` chars). `evaluate.rubric_score(answer, rubric)` → per-item pass/fail with evidence + overall fraction; `run_one` stores it as `result.json` `rubric` and uses its fraction as `score` when there is no ground_truth. `eval_draft.derived_correct` uses the same `number_found`. No LLM judge: `rubric_score(judge=...)` stores a judge result under `judge` without changing the score. The rubric is read only by Box 1 scoring; `tests/test_rubric.py` renders every d19/d24 drafting prompt and every flat and boss_reviewers worker prompt for a task whose rubric holds sentinels and asserts none is sent
spec_table.why: complex tasks have no single right answer; the v1 string match marked a correct GiB/TiB answer wrong; a rubric the team could see would be graded against itself

spec_table.original: AutoAgents runs the steps in list order and gives every helper the whole history (group.py:76 `previous`); `depends_on`, `output` and `done_when` are never used
spec_table.ours: new topology `plan` (`amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py`, `--topology plan`; `run_flat` and `run_boss_reviewers` unchanged as baselines). The step graph comes from `depends_on` (a plan with none is a chain); an unknown step number or a cycle fails validation (V8 plan) before any Box 3 call. A dependency on a step Box 2 dropped (it named no known role; numbers are kept) is re-linked to that step's own dependencies as written, with a `dependency_relinked` event. Steps run in topological waves, sequentially for now; the wave is recorded (`plan_graph`, `step_input`, `step_done` events). Each step's helper sees only the task, a role card (name, goal, skills, constraints, outputs, success criteria, prompt, suggestions), its own step with `do / output / done_when`, and the artifacts of the steps it depends on (`amoeba/config/prompts/plan_step*.txt`, ours); Thought / CurrentStep / Action / ActionInput and the 5-turn cap are kept. Multi-role steps: the roles take turns in roster order within the cap, and a helper that has answered Final Output or BLOCKED is not asked again (flat asks every helper every turn). Each step's result is saved as `runs/<id>/artifacts/step_<n>.md` with `step_<n>.json` (step, wave, roles, covers, depends_on, received, output_spec, status done/blocked/max_turns, turns, sources, contributions) and in `Episode.steps`. The answer is the summariser's step in the last wave. ActionInput is read to the end of the reply (it is the last section): the AutoAgents parser splits on every `##`, so a markdown Final Output is cut at its first `##`/`###` heading — the flat baseline loses most of its answers this way (docs/real_runs/2026-09-24_box3_baseline.md). Plan helpers get `max_tokens` 8192 per call (the D27 retry applies); flat and boss_reviewers keep the client default 2048
spec_table.why: the d24 plan says which step needs which input; passing only those keeps each helper's context on its own job, and the artifacts make each step's contribution inspectable

spec_table.original: AutoAgents routes every drafted tool to SerpAPI (custom_action.py:207-213); Phase 1 had only `echo` and `calc` (D7)
spec_table.ours: `amoeba/tools/web.py`: `web_search(query)` → top results as `[S#] title — url` + snippet and `fetch_url(url or S#)` → the page's clean text, behind a `SearchProvider` interface; the provider is Tavily (`/search`, `/extract` on `api.tavily.com`, key from `TAVILY_API_KEY`). Every result gets a run-wide source id (S1, S2, …; the same url keeps its id) with url, title, kind and time fetched; a plan step's artifact lists its sources. Limits in code and in the trace (`web_tools` event): 5 results per search, 4 searches and 3 fetches per step, 6000 characters per fetched page, 20 s timeout. A failure or a spent limit returns an `error: …` string to the helper with a `tool_error` / `tool_limit` event, never an exception. `run_task --web-tools` builds a fresh Box 3 registry per run; Box 2 never sees the web tools (its envelope is built from `echo`/`calc`), so both plan arms draw from the same drafts. At Box 3 start the plan runner gives `web_search` + `fetch_url` to each role whose missing tools or capability requests normalise (D29) to `web_search` (`capability_mapped` event); the saved team.yaml is unchanged. Tests use a fake provider; `scripts/smoke_web.py` is the one real check
spec_table.why: current facts (prices, laws, benchmarks) need a real lookup; a source id makes each fact traceable (D33)

spec_table.original: (ours) nothing tied a figure in an answer to where it came from
spec_table.ours: the plan-step prompt requires every number, price, date, law or benchmark figure to carry `[S#]` (a tool result) or `[unverified]` (model knowledge); a computed number needs no tag if the calculation is shown or `calc` was used. After each step `amoeba/interp/provenance.py` classifies every number in the step output line by line: cited (the line has a valid `[S#]`), unverified, given (in the task text), derived (a `calc` result or after `=`/`≈` on the line), inherited (already in an input artifact), else untagged. A number is a digit run with optional thousands commas, decimals, a leading currency sign and a trailing %; a letter suffix is not part of it (`$1.45M` → 1.45, `10TB` → 10). List markers and labels (S3, R2, p95, step 4, Phase 1) are not counted. An `[S#]` the step could not have seen is a hallucinated citation; a step can see its own sources and those visible to the steps it depends on (the spec said the step's own sources; inputs carry their tags forward, so their ids count too). Counts go into `step_<n>.json` (`provenance`, `visible_source_ids`), a `provenance` trace event per step, and `result.json` `provenance` {total, steps}. Measured, never enforced
spec_table.why: a model-memory figure should be visible as one; the count of untagged numbers is the size of the invention problem

spec_table.original: (ours) nothing checked a step's output against its `output` / `done_when`, and the d24 verification step was prose
spec_table.ours: after each plan step, deterministic checks (`plan_runner.step_checks`), only those that apply: output present; a markdown table when `output`/`done_when` say table; ≥ 2 list items for list/bullets; a code block or statement for code/script/SQL/schema; ≥ 2 headings for memo/report/runbook/plan/document; a number when they name costs, prices, sizes, rates, benchmarks and the like; and, for a step with dependencies, some use of its inputs (a step number, role name, source id or figure from them, or a line copied from them). A failed check with turns left gets one retry: the reasons are added to the step's work so far and every helper is asked again (`check_retry` event). A step that still fails, or runs out of turns, is `incomplete` with a `status_reason`; the run goes on and later steps see each input's status. A verification step (depends on others and its text says verify/check/review/validate/reconcile, as in draft_quality; not the summariser's step) is told to start its output with `Verdict: PASS|FAIL` and `Issues:`; on FAIL each producer step it depends on is re-run once with the issues and its earlier output (`rework` event; the first version is kept as `step_<n>.first.md`), at most one rework per step, and the verifier is not asked again. Records: `checks`, `retried`, `verification`, `verdict`, `issues`, `rework_of` in each step's metadata and in `Episode.steps` (a reworked step appears twice)
spec_table.why: a plan line that says what done looks like should be checked by code where it can; a verdict that changes nothing is decoration

spec_table.original: AutoAgents' last step (the Language Expert) re-derives and embellishes the answer
spec_table.ours:
the answer step, when the summariser owns it, uses its own prompt (`plan_summarise.txt`, ours): it receives every step's latest output with its status, reason, lacked capabilities, verdict and provenance counts, and the deliverable list from the Box 2 requirements (`TeamConfig.requirements`; never the rubric). It is told to assemble and edit only (no new analysis, facts or numbers; figures copied with their tags), to answer in exactly the form the task asks for (only a value when it asks for a value), to say where a step is missing or incomplete, and — only when there is something to list — to end with `## Limitations` (blocked, partial or incomplete steps, lacked capabilities, main unverified figures). A first Gemini toy run with an always-present Limitations section scored 0/20 ("199

## Limitations
None." is not "199"). Code check (`summary_check`): every figure in the final answer that is in no step output and not in the task is counted as `new_number_in_summary` (examples listed), and whether a Limitations section exists; recorded in the trace and `result.json` `summary_check`
spec_table.why: the summariser has no tools and no sources, so any figure it adds is invented; its job is to carry the team's work to the reader, gaps included

spec_table.original: D21 recorded a BLOCKED step but a blocked helper's partial work and the gap reached no one downstream
spec_table.ours: a plan helper that lacks a capability does the rest and writes `BLOCKED: <capability> — <what could not be done>` in its output (or answers BLOCKED as its action, D21). The step's gaps are the union of both (`plan_runner.blocked_marks`); a step with gaps is `partial` when a helper wrote anything and `incomplete` otherwise, with `status_reason` `lacked: …` and `blocked` / `blocked_canonical` (D29 names) in its metadata. The run always continues; the summariser sees each step's gaps. After the summariser writes, plain code checks that its `## Limitations` section names every lacked capability (canonical name, its spaced form or a name the step used) and appends a `- BLOCKED: <capability> (… added by plain code)` line for each it left out, creating the section if needed (`limitations_added` event, `summary_check.limitations_added_by_code`). `result.json` `blocked_capabilities` counts, per canonical capability, the plan steps (latest version) that lacked it — the input for the later tool-building queue
spec_table.why: a missing capability should shrink the answer, visibly, rather than be papered over with invented results

spec_table.original: **Explicit verification steps.** D34 found verification steps by keywords (verify, check, review …), so "Review current tariff schedules" became a verifier
spec_table.ours: the d24 step format gains `kind: work \| verify` (Planner prompt and format example, `parse_plan_d24`, `DraftPlanStep.kind`, `PlanStep.kind`). The plan runner treats a step as a verifier only when it is `kind: verify`, depends on other steps and is not the summariser's; when the plan declares kinds, an undeclared step is work. Only a plan with no kinds at all (older drafts) falls back to the keyword rule, and each step so judged logs `verification_inferred`. `draft_quality`'s independent-verification check uses the same rule
spec_table.why: a word in a step title is not a decision; the planner says which steps check others

spec_table.original: **Check again after rework.** D34 reworked the producer steps after a FAIL but never asked the verifier again, so a fixed step still reached the summariser under a FAIL verdict
spec_table.ours: after the producer steps are reworked, the verifier runs once more with a `RE-CHECK` note (its earlier issues and which steps were reworked); no further rework follows, whatever the second verdict. The verifier's metadata keeps `verdict_first` and `verdict_after_rework`; `verdict` is always the latest, and the summariser sees e.g. "verdict: PASS (after rework; first verdict FAIL)". The first verifier output is kept as `step_<n>.first.md`; a `reverify` event names the reworked steps
spec_table.why: a rework is only worth something if someone checks it; the answer should carry the verdict that applies to what it uses

spec_table.original: **Stale inputs after rework.** A step that ran on a producer's first output kept using it after the producer was reworked, and nothing said so
spec_table.ours: after a verifier's FAIL reworks producer steps (D34/D38), every step that already ran and depends on a reworked step directly or through other steps — except that verifier, which checks again — is marked `stale` with `stale_because` in its metadata (rewritten on disk) and a `stale` trace event. `run_task --rerun-stale` (default off) re-runs each stale step once, in plan order, on the reworked inputs (`rerun_of_stale`; the old version kept as `step_<n>.first.md`). Later steps see "STALE (built on step(s) … before their rework)" on that input and the summariser sees "STALE: …". Plan-runner settings travel as `PlanOptions` (`Interpreter(plan_options=…)`), all recorded in the `plan_graph` event
spec_table.why: an answer built on outputs that were later corrected should say so, and re-running is a cost the user chooses

spec_table.original: **The answer step is not a blocked step.** D36 scanned every step's output for `BLOCKED:` lines, including the summariser's Limitations section, which names the producers' gaps on purpose — so a good final answer was marked partial and its gaps were counted twice
spec_table.ours: the answer step is never scanned for BLOCKED: its status is `done` unless it ran out of turns or failed a check. The names it mentions are kept as `blocked_mentions` (information only); `blocked` stays empty and the step carries `answer_step: true`. `blocked_capabilities` in result.json and the capabilities the Limitations section must name count producer steps only
spec_table.why: a step's status says what that step failed to do; reporting other steps' gaps is the answer step's job

spec_table.original: **Answer put together by code when no one writes it.** D31 took the last step of the last wave as the answer, so when the last wave held several steps and the summariser owned none of them, all but one step's output was dropped
spec_table.ours: when the summariser owns a step in the last wave, that step is the answer (D35); when the last wave has one step, it is; otherwise plain code assembles the answer from every last-wave step in plan order, one `## Step <n>: <title>` heading each, then completes the Limitations section with the producers' lacked capabilities (D36). Recorded as `answer_assembled_by_code` (the step numbers) in result.json, an `answer_assembled_by_code` trace event and `artifacts/answer.md`; the run's error is the worst status among those steps
spec_table.why: no step's work is dropped silently, and no AI is asked to write what code can put together

spec_table.original: **Checks from the planner's format markers.** D34 guessed format checks from words in `output`/`done_when` ("plan", "report", "cost"…), accepted any copied line as "using the inputs", and allowed a retry only when turns were left
spec_table.ours: the d24 prompt asks each step's `output` line to start with one or more markers — `table:`, `list:`, `code:`, `memo:` — and the format checks come from those (a table, ≥ 2 list items, a code block or statement, ≥ 2 headings); only an `output` line with no marker falls back to the D34 keyword rules. Each check records its `source` (markers/keywords) and the step its `check_source`. `inputs_referenced` now needs a real match: a figure from an input (not a single digit), one of its source ids, a dependency's step number or role name, or 8 consecutive shared words; a whole output under 8 words copied from an input (a value) still counts, a copied line inside other text no longer does. A failed check's retry gets its own `check_retry_turns` (default 2) on top of the turns used
spec_table.why: the planner says what each step must produce, so code checks exactly that; a check that anything passes checks nothing

spec_table.original: **Figure ledger.** D33 judged each step's numbers on their own line, so a figure that entered untagged was counted "inherited" (clean) as soon as a later step or the summary copied it
spec_table.ours: the plan runner keeps a ledger of every figure in the run: its first status (cited / unverified / untagged / derived / given), the step that first wrote it and its sources (`provenance.check_provenance` now returns each figure's status). A later step or the summary that repeats a figure inherits that first status: each step records `figure_origins` (its figures counted by ledger status), and `summary_check` adds `answer_figures`, `answer_cited`, `answer_unverified` and `answer_untagged` (the figures in the final answer by their first status). The ledger is written to result.json (`figure_ledger`) and summarised in a `figure_ledger` trace event
spec_table.why: copying a number does not make it any more sourced; the answer should be judged by where its figures first came from

spec_table.original: **Size limits on what a step is shown.** D31 passed every input artifact whole, the summariser saw every output whole, and a step that never gave a Final Output passed on its entire work log
spec_table.ours: a step with no Final Output passes on only its last helper message. Each input artifact shown to a step is cut at `max_input_chars` (default 6,000; `run_task --max-input-chars`); the summariser's inputs are cut the same way and, when together they would pass `max_summary_input_chars` (default 30,000; `--max-summary-input-chars`), each step's output gets an equal share (at least 500). A cut keeps the beginning and ends with "[... cut by plain code: first N of M characters shown]", with an `input_truncated` trace event (step, source step, limit, length); both limits are in the `plan_graph` event
spec_table.why: prompt size, and so cost, must not grow with how much the previous step wrote; a cut must be visible to the helper and in the trace

spec_table.original: **Reuse saved drafts.** Every run drafted its team again, so comparing Box 3 arms paid for Box 2 each time and each arm ran on a different draft
spec_table.ours: `run_task --drafts-from DIR [--draft-pick K]` reuses a saved Box 2 draft instead of drafting (`amoeba/task/saved_drafts.py`): DIR is an eval_draft output folder (read directly: `drafts/<task>.<n>.json`) or a runs folder (`<run_id>/plan.json`, or `draft.json` when present; one run folder works too). Each task takes its K-th saved draft (repeat order for eval_draft, run start order for runs); failed drafts are skipped, and a task with no K-th draft is skipped with a message. `plan.json` already holds the whole draft; `team.yaml` is not reused because it is built per topology, so every topology builds its team from the same draft. No drafting call is made; a `draft_reused` event and result.json `draft_source` (the eval_draft file stem or the run id) record where it came from
spec_table.why: the arms of a comparison should differ only in Box 3, and a draft already paid for should not be paid for again

spec_table.original: **Response cache.** Every evaluation paid the model (and the search provider) again for identical calls, and a run could not be repeated offline
spec_table.ours: `amoeba/llm/cache.py`: `--llm-cache DIR` stores every LLM reply under a hash of (model, messages, max_tokens, temperature) plus an optional `--llm-cache-namespace` (e.g. the repeat number, so repeats of one prompt are not collapsed; the seed is not keyed), and every web_search / fetch_url result under a hash of (provider, operation, query or url, max_results, namespace). `--llm-cache-mode record` answers from the cache when it can and otherwise calls and stores; `replay` answers only from the cache — a miss raises `CacheMiss`, the run stops with `error="cache_miss: …"` (a `cache_miss` event) and nothing reaches the network (the web provider is not even built, so no key is needed); `off` passes through. A replayed reply is marked `amoeba.cache_hit` on its chat span. The same flags exist on eval_draft (shared `add_client_args`)
spec_table.why: a result that was paid for once can be re-scored, re-analysed and re-run for free, and replay proves a run used nothing new

spec_table.original: **Per-run limits and a cost estimate.** Spec §2 recorded tokens and never enforced them; a runaway run could only be stopped by the provider's spending cap (it was, on 2026-09-24)
spec_table.ours: opt-in limits in `amoeba/llm/limits.py`: `run_task --max-tokens-per-run N` / `--max-calls-per-run N` are checked by `TracedLLM` before every call (billed tokens = input + output + reasoning of live calls; cache hits (D46) are free and do not count). When a limit is reached the call is not made, a `budget_stop` event is logged, and the run ends with `error="budget"` — the draft, every finished plan step, the trace and result.json are saved. With no limit set nothing reads the token count (T9 now allows the word only in this module and checks that an unlimited run is never stopped). After every run the CLI prints its billed tokens and an estimated cost from `amoeba/config/prices.yaml` (US$ per 1M tokens, reasoning priced as output; shipped with null prices to fill in — a model without a price gets tokens only); result.json `usage` holds the same
spec_table.why: the user decides the most a run may spend; stopping cleanly keeps what was already paid for

spec_table.original: **Wait out rate limits.** The OpenAI SDK retried twice on its own, invisibly; run_task gave up on the next 429; only eval_draft had a (fixed-wait) retry
spec_table.ours: `OpenAICompatibleClient` turns the SDK's retries off and retries HTTP 429 and 503 itself: up to `--max-rate-retries` (default 5) times, waiting the server's `Retry-After` when given, else 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s (capped at 60). A 429 that names a spending cap is not retried (it will not clear in seconds), nor is any other error. Each wait is a `rate_limited` trace event (status, wait, attempt, Retry-After, whether it finally gave up) and the chat span carries `amoeba.rate_limit_retries`. `--min-seconds-between-calls` (default 0) spaces model calls out for free tiers (`amoeba.throttle_wait_s`). eval_draft's own retry now covers only HTTP 500
spec_table.why: free and paid tiers both throttle; waiting is cheaper than losing a half-done run, and every wait should be visible

spec_table.original: **Gemma 4 support.** The client always sent a system message and never a reasoning setting; Gemma models served through the Gemini API do not take a system instruction
spec_table.ours: two `OpenAICompatibleClient` options, on run_task and eval_draft: `--merge-system` puts the system message at the top of the first user message (or makes it the user message) and sends no system role (`client.merge_system`); `--reasoning-effort off\|low\|medium\|high` is sent as `reasoning_effort` only when set, `off` as `none` (the value Gemini's OpenAI-compatible layer takes to turn thinking off). Both are part of the response-cache key (D46). README: how to run Gemma 4 through the Gemini API and through OpenRouter
spec_table.why: a model that cannot take a system role still gets the whole prompt; thinking is a cost the user can turn down

spec_table.original: **Self-refinement from evidence.** D42 gave a step one retry only when a format or input check failed; untagged figures and citations of unseen sources were counted but never shown to the helper
spec_table.ours: `run_task --self-refine off\|on-issues\|always` (CLI default `on-issues`). After a step's helpers finish, plain code collects its findings — failed checks (D34/D42) and, unless `off`, provenance findings (D33): untagged figures (with examples) and citations of sources the step never saw. With any finding the helper(s) get one refine turn listing exactly those findings, with their own `check_retry_turns` (2) on top of the step's turns. `always` adds a self-review turn against the step's `done_when` and the roles' success criteria when nothing was found. `off` is the earlier D42 behaviour (failed checks only), and the library default (`PlanOptions.self_refine = "off"`) so callers that set nothing are unchanged. Each step records `refine_reason` (checks / provenance / checks+provenance / self_review) and `refine` {findings, before, after} with counts of failed checks, untagged figures and hallucinated citations; a `refine` trace event carries the same; result.json `refinement` sums them for the run
spec_table.why: the helper should fix what code can prove is wrong, and only that; the before/after counts show whether it did

spec_table.original: **Collaborative refinement in multi-role steps.** D31 had every role of a step write on its own and joined the outputs under per-role headings, so a step's roles never checked each other's work
spec_table.ours: `run_task --collab concat\|critique` (CLI default `critique`). `critique`: the step's first role (roster order) drafts the step output with the step's turns; each other role then replies with the review prompt (`plan_critique.txt`, ours) — `AGREE`, or `REVISE` with numbered issues judged against the step's `done_when` and its own success criteria, no new analysis; on any REVISE the drafter revises with every issue listed, with turns of its own (2). At most `collab_rounds` (2) review rounds; plain code ends it when all AGREE or the rounds run out (the last revision is then not reviewed). An unreadable review counts as AGREE and is logged (`review_unreadable`). The step's output is the drafter's one text. `concat` keeps the earlier behaviour, for the ablation, and is the library default (`PlanOptions.collab`). Each step records `collab` {drafter, reviewers, rounds, revisions, objections per role per round, agreed}; `collab_round` trace events; result.json `refinement` adds collab steps, agreements and rounds. Self-refinement (D50) then applies to the drafter
spec_table.why: a step owned by several roles should produce one answer they have all checked, and whether they agreed is worth knowing

spec_table.original: **Task intake check.** The Planner's Requirements and Givens were compared with the plan and the roles (D24 `requirements_covered`), never with the task itself, so a number the task gave or a deliverable it asked for could drop out of the draft (or a "test" become an "estimate") unseen
spec_table.ours: `draft_quality` check 8 `task_coverage` (`amoeba/task/quality.py::task_coverage`, given the task text): every number the task states (`provenance.claim_numbers`: list markers and labels such as "step 3" left out; "5,000" = "5000") must appear in a requirement or a given; every deliverable-like phrase — one of deliver, estimate, assess, prototype, test, gather, build, plan (any inflection) and up to six words after it, cut at punctuation or and/then/or/but/so — must map to a requirement that uses the same verb and, when the phrase names an object, shares a content word with it. The check records `numbers`, `missing_numbers`, `phrases` and `missing_phrases`; n/a on a d19 draft (no requirement ids). Recorded only (Draft.quality, result.json, the `draft_quality` event); it is a hard check, so `--quality-gate` sends a draft that misses one back with the missing numbers and phrases listed
spec_table.why: the draft must carry the whole task before anyone plans from it, and D24's own rule ("keep the task's own verbs") is now checked by code

spec_table.original: **Open questions, and an optional look before the team runs.** D24 told the Planner "do not ask the user questions; state assumptions instead", so an ambiguity it settled was mixed into the givens, and no one could correct it before Box 3 spent the budget
spec_table.ours: the d24 Planner prompt and format example (ours) gain an optional `## Open Questions` section: each ambiguity it settled by assumption, as `- question: ... \| assumption: ...` (None when nothing was ambiguous). It is not a required section, so a reply without it costs no repair call. `parsers.parse_open_questions` reads it (the assumption may also sit on its own line under the question; an echoed format example is dropped) into `Draft.open_questions` [{question, assumption}]. `run_task --interactive` (default off; not on eval_draft or any eval script; refused with `--drafts-from`): after Box 2 it prints the requirements, the givens that are assumptions and the open questions, and waits: `continue` runs the draft; any other line is appended to the task as `User clarification: ...` and the Planner, shown its previous draft as history, gets one more round (`draft_team(max_rounds=1, history=...)`) whose draft is used. An empty line asks again; end of input means continue. The first draft is kept as plan.first.json; an `intake_review` event and result.json `clarification` record what happened
spec_table.why: an assumption the user can correct in one line is cheaper than a run built on the wrong one; evaluations stay unattended

spec_table.original: **Model profiles; Gemma is the default real model.** A real model was chosen by --base-url/--model or AMOEBA_* variables with a gpt-4o-mini fallback, every call of a run used that one model, and the trace wrote the model the API returned in place of the model asked for
spec_table.ours: `amoeba/config/models.yaml` (next to prices.yaml, per the §3 layout, rather than a top-level config/) holds named profiles: `gemma-api` (the default: Gemini API endpoint, `gemma-4-31b-it`, merge_system, reasoning_effort low), `gemma-openrouter` (`google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`, merge_system) and `gemini-flash-lite` / `gemini-flash` (the baseline settings). A profile sets base_url, model, api_key_env, merge_system, reasoning_effort, max_tokens and, per role group (planner, observers, workers, reviewers, summariser), a model and max_tokens; an unknown key or group is an error. `run_task` and `eval_draft --profile NAME` (shared `add_client_args`) apply with `--llm openai`; `--llm mock` stays the default and is never routed. --base-url/--model > AMOEBA_BASE_URL/AMOEBA_MODEL > the profile (per-role models still apply); --api-key > AMOEBA_API_KEY > the profile's api_key_env > OPENAI_API_KEY; --[no-]merge-system and --reasoning-effort (`unset` sends nothing) > the profile; --planner/--observer-max-tokens > the profile's group max_tokens > AMOEBA_MAX_TOKENS_* > 8192. `amoeba/llm/profiles.py`: `RoleRouter` holds one client per distinct model (each cached when --llm-cache is set) and `TracedLLM` routes each call by its role group (Box 2 by caller; Box 3 by the helper: critic or verify step or critique review = reviewers, the summariser role = summariser, else workers); a group's max_tokens replaces the call's own (not on the D27 retry). Every trace line carries `amoeba.profile`; each chat span `amoeba.role_group`, `gen_ai.request.model` (asked for) and `gen_ai.response.model` (the exact name the API returned — it used to overwrite the request model). result.json: `profile`, `models` {requested per group, returned}; the cost estimate prices each call by its own model. eval_draft rows add `profile` and `models_returned`. `scripts/list_models.py` prints the models an endpoint lists and marks or reports the profile's; README: switching profiles, and that model names must be checked against the provider
spec_table.why: Gemma is the model to run on; which model did the work must be in every record, and a role that needs a stronger model should not force it on every call

spec_table.original: **A self-updating as-built page at minimum token cost.** The as-built page was rebuilt by hand; its box text was hand-written in `BOXES` and went stale silently; which code a box covered lived only in `BOXES`; trace lines did not say which box wrote them, so only the offline sample runs could be replayed
spec_table.ours: (1) **Tags:** a `# box: <id>[, <id>]` comment above a def or class puts that code in the box; the 106 existing `BOXES` anchors were tagged. `tools/arch_extract.py` exits 2 on a tag that names no box or is not above a def/class, on a `BOXES` anchor that resolves to nothing or lacks its tag, and on a trace table naming an unknown box; tagged code `BOXES` does not list joins its box; untagged top-level code new since the last build is listed as "unassigned" (older untagged helpers are shown folded). (2) **Text cache:** `tools/arch_text.py` keeps each box's `sentence` and `what` in `docs/arch/box_text.json` with a hash of the box's facts (anchor signatures, docstrings, fields, callees, guards, check messages, prompt-text hashes, number names; no line numbers, no number values). Same hash: reused, no call. Hand text in `BOXES` edited: used as is, no call. Facts changed: one call to the `arch-text` profile (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, 700-token replies) with the numbered old text, the diff of the facts and the facts: reply `keep`, or `rewrite` with line edits only (every other line kept word for word); an unusable reply, an API error or no key keeps the old text and marks the box stale for the next rebuild. Every rebuild appends calls and tokens to `docs/arch/text_log.jsonl`; the page shows each box's text source. (3) **Numbers:** digits in the text that equal exactly one number the box's code names (a module constant it uses, a numeric field or parameter default it defines or reads) become `{NAME}` placeholders, filled from the extracted values at every build; a model rewrite that writes a number the code does not hold is rejected. (4) **Trace:** `TraceWriter` stamps `amoeba.box` on every span and event (`SPAN_BOX`, `EVENT_BOX`, the Box 2 callers, the box of the innermost open span; each invoke_agent span names its box); the page replays the newest real run under `runs/` (`--replay-run=DIR` or `ARCH_REPLAY_RUN` to choose) and lists boxes with no line and lines with no box. (5) **Hooks:** `tools/arch_update.py` hashes every input and rebuilds only on change (stamp in `docs/arch/build_stamp.json`, one rebuild at a time, never fails its caller); run by `tools/hooks/post-commit` (`git config core.hooksPath tools/hooks`) and by the Stop hook in `.claude/settings.json`, both detached
spec_table.why: the page must follow the code without anyone remembering to rebuild it, and a rebuild with nothing new must cost nothing

spec_table.original: **Box 3 stocks its toolbox from an open tool/skill pool.** Box 2 recorded every tool or skill the team asked for and did not get (capability_requests.json) and nothing acted on it ("Nothing is fetched or built: that is a later phase"), so a helper could only answer BLOCKED
spec_table.ours: (1) **Pool index** (`amoeba/pool/index.py`, 0 tokens): `python -m amoeba pool refresh` (console script `amoeba`) reads the sources in `amoeba/config/pool.yaml` — the official MCP Registry API (`/v0/servers`, cursor pagination, per server name the version marked isLatest, else the newest published; inactive servers left out) and github.com/anthropics/skills (the repository itself: a fork or a renamed repository is refused; every `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` at the default branch's current commit, YAML frontmatter then body) — into `data/pool/index.json` plus one `skills/*.md` per body. Per entry: id, name, description, kind, source, source repo URL, version (a skill: the commit), remote URL and transport (the first HTTPS streamable-http/SSE remote), whether a key is needed (a required or secret header, or a URL variable), has_scripts (a `scripts/` directory, an executable file, or a code file), body length, sha256 of the description, refreshed_at. A failing source is reported and the others are still written. Runs read only this cache. (2) **Match** (`pool/match.py`, 0 tokens): pool entries of the request's kind are scored by the content words they share with the request's standard name and its aliases (`aliases.yaml`), raw name, what it does, input and output (a word in the entry's name or title counts once more); the top 5 are kept. None above zero → unfilled `no_candidates`, no AI call. (3) **Pick**: one call per request (deduplicated by kind, standard name and helper) in the new `pool` role group (a profile's `roles.pool`, else the workers' model), prompt `pool_pick.txt` (ours): the request (name, kind, what it does, input, output, helper, its step lines) and the candidates (id, name, one-line description, kind, inside a POOL DATA block); reply exactly one listed id or NONE. Parsed strictly: the reply, stripped of whitespace and wrapping quotes/backticks, must equal a listed id; anything else is `pick_none`. The call goes through TracedLLM, so `--llm-cache` and the run limits apply. (4) **Vet** (`pool/stock.py::vet`, the first failing rule is recorded): tools — an HTTPS streamable-http/SSE remote (`not_remote`), a source repository (`no_source`), a pinned version (`no_version`: semver-like, not "latest"), no key needed or the key in the environment variable pool.yaml names for that server (`auth_missing`), the description's sha256 equal to the one stored at refresh (`description_changed`); then it is connected and its tools/list must match the pins in `data/pool/pins.json` (`description_changed`; a server attached for the first time is pinned then — trust on first use, the only file a run writes in the cache), an unreachable server is `connect_failed`. Skills — no scripts (`has_scripts`), body ≤ 5,000 characters (`too_long`), body file present (`body_missing`). Caps: 3 pool items per helper, 8 per run (`cap_reached`). A request with no helper to give it to is `no_helper`; one a registered tool already covers (e.g. web_search with --web-tools, D32) is `registered_tool`, without a pick. (5) **Attach**: the step runs in `run_one` after instantiate and before `Interpreter.run` picks the runner. A tool becomes `pool:<server name>` in a copy of the run's ToolRegistry (`ToolRegistry.copy`; the shared registry is untouched) and in the asking helper's tools only; `ToolRegistry.execute` stays the one place it runs: `PoolTools.call` opens a connection with the official MCP Python SDK (`mcp>=2.2`, a new dependency), lists the tools again and refuses a changed description before calling (`tool_error`, reason `description_changed`), with web_search's limits — 3 calls per step, 20 s, 6,000 result characters (pool.yaml) — and an `error: ...` line, never a crash, on any failure. One server is one tool: plain text goes to its one string argument when it has one tool, a JSON object is its arguments, and a server with several tools takes `{"tool": ..., "arguments": {...}}`. Every result gets a source id [S#] (the same numbering as web_search when the run has it), so the plan runner's provenance counts a figure taken from it as cited. A skill's SKILL.md body goes on that helper's role card (`role_card`, `plan_card`) under `Skill: <name> (from <repo>@<commit>)`. All pool text — candidate descriptions, tool descriptions, tool results, skill bodies — reaches a prompt only inside `<<<POOL DATA · ...>>> ... <<<END POOL DATA>>>` blocks that say it is reference data (an end marker inside the text is defused). A filled request's "Tool X is unavailable this run" line is removed (it leaves `missing_tools`); an unfilled one keeps today's behaviour (the helper may answer BLOCKED: X). Topologies: flat and plan helpers see pool tools in their tool list with their description; boss + reviewers has no tool actions, so only skills change it — on a critic's card through `role_description`, and after the solver's system prompt, because the verbatim AgentVerse solver prompt has no card slot. (6) **Record**: each request in capability_requests.json (and result.json requested_capabilities) gains `status` filled/unfilled, `pool_id` picked, `candidates` shown, `reason` code; with no cache every request is `pool_unavailable`, and a request raised during the run is `raised_during_run`. result.json `pool` {status ran/unavailable/off, filled, unfilled, llm_calls, reasons, attached}; trace events pool_unavailable, pool_match, pool_vet, pool_pinned, pool_connect_failed, pool_summary (box `toolbox`), pool_call (box `tools`); the pick is a chat span in the `stock_toolbox` span, role group `pool`. `run_task --pool/--no-pool` (default on; `--no-pool` for replaying an older `--llm-cache`) and `--pool-dir`; `run_one(pool=None)` (the library default) skips the step. Without a cache the run logs `pool_unavailable` and makes exactly the calls it made before
spec_table.why: LLM proposes, plain code disposes: the only AI decision is which of a few matched candidates fits, and everything that could hurt the run — where code comes from, keys, changed descriptions, scripts, size, how often a tool runs — is decided by code before and during every call

spec_table.original: **Gemma runs without flags; a failing service ends a run with its records.** The first real Gemma run (gemma-api profile) failed on its first call with HTTP 400 "Thinking level is not supported for this model" because the profile sent reasoning_effort low (it had to be run with `--reasoning-effort unset`); a dropped connection (APIConnectionError through the proxy) was not retried — D48 retried only 429/503 — and ended the process, so the run left no result.json
spec_table.ours: `gemma-api` no longer sets reasoning_effort. `OpenAICompatibleClient` retries a dropped connection or a timeout (the SDK's APIConnectionError / APITimeoutError, matched by class name, or Python's ConnectionError / TimeoutError) exactly like a 429/503: the same waits (2·2^n s, max 60), the same 5-retry cap, each wait a `rate_limited` line now carrying `amoeba.dropped` connection/timeout. An error from the service still there after the retries (`llm.client.api_error`: an HTTP status, a dropped connection, a timeout) ends the run cleanly: in Box 3 `Interpreter.run` sets `error = "api: <class> <status>: <message>"` and keeps what ran; while drafting or in the pool pick, `run_one` does the same; an `api_error` trace line (box `client`) is written, and plan.json, capability_requests.json and result.json are always written. Any other exception (a bug) still raises
spec_table.why: a real run must start with the shipped defaults, and an outage an hour into a run must leave records to resume from (`--llm-cache` replays the calls already paid for), not a stack trace

spec_table.original: **Pool-side fixes before observer round 2.** The D56 skills refresh used the GitHub REST API, which a Claude Code cloud session's GitHub proxy refuses for a repository not attached to the session (HTTP 403), so the pool had 0 skills; and the matcher compared a request only with pool entries of the kind the Planner wrote, while round 1 showed the Planner never writes "skill" (0 of 23 requests — xlsx, docx, pptx and brand style all asked as tools), so no skill could ever be a candidate
spec_table.ours: (1) `pool/index.py::repo_skills` reads skills from a shallow `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/<repo>` (`git_clone`, LFS pointers not fetched) into a temporary folder: the commit is the clone's HEAD; every `<path>/<name>/SKILL.md` directly under the path is a skill; `has_scripts` = a `scripts/` folder anywhere in the skill, an executable file or a code file; only the repository named in pool.yaml is cloned, and the clone's origin must be exactly `https://github.com/<repo>`, else the source fails (the GitHub API's fork flag is no longer read). anthropics/skills at 33375500: 19 skills, 9 instruction-only (3 of them ≤ 5,000 characters: brand-guidelines, internal-comms, theme-factory; xlsx, docx, pptx and pdf ship scripts). (2) `pool/match.py::rank` scores tools and skills alike and keeps the top 5 overall; the `pool_match` event lists each candidate's kind, `pool_vet` adds `amoeba.kind_requested` and `amoeba.kind_picked`, and result.json `pool.attached` adds `kind_requested`. What is attached still follows the picked entry's kind (a tool request filled by a skill puts the skill on the card and removes the request's "unavailable" line). (3) Two more vetting rules, read-only tools only for now: `side_effect` — a tool whose name, title or description names an outside action (send, email, mail, post, publish, pay, payment, purchase, delete, "write to"; names split at - _ . /), checked on the pool entry and again on every tool the server lists when it is connected; `paid_endpoint` — a remote host equal to or under a domain in pool.yaml `paid_hosts` (shipped: `*.klymax402.com`, pay-per-call x402 endpoints). (4) The picker's reply is read after any closed `<thought>…</thought>` / `<think>…</think>` block: Gemma writes its reasoning into the reply text before the id, so the first round-2 run parsed a correct pick (`io.github.lu-zhengda/mcp-python-exec-sandbox`) as NONE; the rest of the reply must still equal a listed id, and an unclosed block gives NONE. With `--pool off` nothing here runs, so a run is unchanged
spec_table.why: round 2 must be able to use skills at all, and a capability should be found whatever kind the Planner guessed for it

spec_table.original: **Local tools: Amoeba borrows Claude Code's tools and skills through `claude mcp serve`.** In observer rounds 1 and 2 no helper could run code or write a file (tasks 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10), and the pool could not help: its code runners and Office-format servers are local packages or paid, and the xlsx / docx / pptx / pdf skills are refused because they ship scripts
spec_table.ours: (1) **Connect** (`amoeba/localtools/`, `--local-tools on|off`, default off; `run_one(local=LocalSetup)`): `claude mcp serve` is started once per run over stdio with the MCP Python SDK (`server.py::StdioServer`: the session lives on an event loop in a background thread; closed at the end of the run, whatever happened), cwd `runs/<id>/workspace/`, environment PATH (this Python first), a private HOME (deleted at the end), `LANG`, `MPLBACKEND=Agg`, no keys and no proxy settings, so no model can be called. Only Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep are allowed (`localtools.yaml`); every other tool the server lists is refused and logged once (`local_tool_refused`, reason not_allowed), an allowed tool the server does not list is logged once (`local_tool_missing`: Claude Code 2.1.283 offers no Glob or Grep). Allowed tools become `local:<Name>` in the run's ToolRegistry copy, run through `ToolRegistry.execute`. (2) **Sandbox and gate** (`gate.py`, plain code, before every call): the feature needs `AMOEBA_SANDBOX=1` (checked by `run_task` and by `LocalToolbox`); every path argument must resolve, symlinks followed, inside the workspace (`outside_workspace`); a Bash command is prefixed with `cd <workspace> &&`, and refused as `network_command` (curl, wget, ssh, scp, nc, git clone/push/fetch/pull, pip/npm/apt install, Python network imports) or `unsafe_command` (sudo, rm on / ~ * or .., cd out, ../, ~/ and $HOME, an absolute path outside the workspace such as /etc, ln -s, kill, chmod/chown on system paths, mkfs, dd, eval) — a screen for the plain cases; the containment is the sandbox the operator vouches for. 60 s per call, 8,000 characters of output, 20 calls per step, 60 per run (`step_cap`, `run_cap`); a JSON input a tool needs and did not get is `bad_input`. Every call (`local_call`: tool, command or path, decision, characters, error, files it changed, ms) and every refusal (`local_refused`: tool, command or path, reason) is a trace line (box `localtools`); a file's content is never logged. openpyxl 3.1.5, python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, matplotlib 3.11.2 and pypdf 6.19.0 are installed in the environment, not at run time. (3) **Skills** (`skills.py`): listed from Claude Code's skill folders (`~/.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills`) and the anthropics/skills clone that `pool refresh` now keeps whole under `<pool cache>/repos/` (`repo_skills(keep=…)`); with the flag on, the index's own skill entries are left out (the clone stands for them) and `has_scripts` no longer refuses: an attached skill's folder is copied to `workspace/skills/<name>/` (symlinks left out) and its SKILL.md frontmatter plus the first 5,000 characters of the body go on the helper's card, inside a POOL DATA block, then "Full skill files are in skills/<name>/; read them with local:Read if needed."; the helper also gets local:Read, Bash, Write and Edit. With the flag off the D56/D58 rules are unchanged. (4) **Matching**: local tools and skills are candidates with source `local`, listed before the pool's for the same request (the picker still chooses; `pool_match` marks them). An alias whose words all appear in the request's name or standard name puts its item first: code runner / python interpreter / code execution → local:Bash; file writing / save file → local:Write; excel / spreadsheet → xlsx; presentation / powerpoint → pptx; word document / word doc → docx; pdf reader / pdf → pdf; then keyword matches. Vetting of a local item: `local_unavailable` (no server), `not_exposed`, `body_missing`. With `--no-pool` only local items are candidates. (5) **Claims** (`claims.py`, plan runner): a sentence of a step's output (code blocks and BLOCKED lines left out) with a file name, a claim verb (saved, created, wrote, generated, exported …) and no negation or future is a claim; a claimed file that is not in the workspace makes the step `incomplete`, reason `claimed_file_missing: <files>` (event `claimed_file_missing`; step meta `claimed_files`, `claimed_files_missing`). result.json gains `files_created` [{path, size, step}], `local_tool_calls`, `local_refusals` {reason: n}, `skills_attached` [{id, name, root, path, helpers}], and `pool.local` {server, exposed, …}; the workspace (without skills/) is copied to `artifacts/files/`. With the flag off none of these fields, events, folders or checks exist and the prompts and calls are the same as before
spec_table.why: Round 1 showed code running and file writing as the largest gaps; the pool refuses skills with scripts; Claude Code's tools give a sandboxed runner without calling Claude's model

spec_table.original: **Pick fixes, a wider read-only rule, clone-only skills.** Observer round 2 (`docs/eval/round2/`) filled 2 of 20 requests: the picker chose an id that vetting then refused 13 times out of 15 (P2), often while a passing candidate was on the same list; 3 of 20 pick replies were cut off at the 2,048-token default with no id (P1: `pick()` set no max_tokens, so the D27 retry never ran); `side_effect` let through a tool that creates decks in the vendor's account (P6); and the local skill listing (D59) included the user's own synced skills from `~/.claude/skills`
spec_table.ours: (1) **Vet before the pick** (`pool/stock.py::stock_toolbox`): up to `vet_depth` (pool.yaml: 50) keyword matches — local items first when --local-tools is on — are vetted with the same rules as before, and the picker is shown only the best `max_candidates` (5) that pass; the `pool_match` event lists them and every refused one with its reason (`amoeba.pool.refused`). None pass → unfilled `all_refused`, no AI call (none matched at all → `no_candidates`, as before). The pick's verdict is the one already computed; the connect-time checks (pins, the server's tools/list, side_effect on every listed tool) and the caps still run after the pick. (2) **Reply room and one retry**: `pick()` sends `max_tokens` = pool.yaml `pick_max_tokens` (6,000) unless the profile's `roles.pool.max_tokens` sets one; a reply cut off there (`finish_reason: length`) is asked once more with twice the room (TracedLLM, D27), and whatever then comes is parsed strictly as before. (3) **`side_effect` widened**: a tool whose name, title or description creates, updates, uploads, modifies, edits, inserts, removes, renames, submits, writes, overwrites or appends — anything in an outside service or account — is refused too (on the pool entry and on every tool the server lists); nouns common in read-only descriptions ("updates", "share", "schedule", "moving") are not in the list. On the cached pool: 5,469 of 35,703 tools refused (D58's words: 3,832). A deck, doc or sheet is made locally with local tools instead. (4) **Skills from the anthropics/skills clone only**: `localtools.yaml` `skill_roots: []` — the user's `~/.claude/skills` and a project `.claude/skills` are no longer listed (a folder can be added back there). No pipeline (Box 1–3 runner) code changes
spec_table.why: round 2 showed the pool failing in the pick, not in the pool: a picker that only sees what code will accept, and has room to answer, can only choose something usable; and the pool stays read-only, with anything made or changed done in the sandboxed workspace

spec_table.original: **The step contract: Box 3 judges a step by evidence, not by the helper's word (closes gaps G1–G7).** Observer rounds 1–3 (`docs/eval/round3/report.md`) held C1–C5 near 35/50. Giving the team capabilities raised what it could do, but a step was still "done" whenever the helper said so. The run recorded unfilled requests, tool calls, files and sources, and the code judging steps and assembling the answer never read them (G1–G7 on the as-built page). Round 3 also found local items crowding out better internet ones (P14) and fenced Bash commands (P17)
spec_table.ours: `--step-contract on` (the CLI default; library default `off`, `PlanOptions.contract`), in `interp/plan_runner.py`. **Contract**: before a step, `contract()` lists per helper (i) `needs`: its missing tools plus its capability requests that are neither filled (`status`, handed over by `run_task` after the toolbox step) nor covered by a tool it has, and (ii) `items`: each pool tool, and its local tools and local skills as one item. A pool skill is card text and needs no call. The list goes on the helper's prompt. **Evidence**: every tool call is recorded (agent, tool, ok = not an error / refusal / error result). **G1**: a need with no `BLOCKED:` and no `NOT NEEDED: <name> — why` line (names matched by canonical form) → one refine turn naming it, then a gap: `partial`, "lacked: X; not declared by the helper: X" (the answer step included). **G2**: an item with no successful call and no such line → the same refine turn ("never called it" / "every call to it failed"), then `partial`, "attached unused: X". Contract findings earn the D50 refine turn whatever `--self-refine` says, sharing it with the other findings. NOT NEEDED lines go to `not_needed` and are removed from the text. **G3**: `enforce_limitations` also appends undeclared gaps (the answer step's own too) and `- NOT USED: X (given to the team for step N but never used; added by plain code)`, matched by canonical name. **G4**: a verify step's inputs carry per checked step its sources, tool calls, figure counts, files made and gaps (`evidence_text`). **G5**: the answer step is told the files each step made; files and source-cited figures (2+ digits) missing from the answer earn one refine turn; files still unnamed are inserted by code under "## Files made" (before Limitations; also in `assemble_by_code`); `summary_check` records `files_listed_by_code` and `cited_figures_left_out`. **G6**: each step records `causes` (capability, checks, max_turns, unused_tool, claimed_file_missing); a producer whose only cause is `capability` is not reworked (`rework_skipped`). **G7**: `LocalToolbox.call` registers a successful result in the run's one source list (`local.book` = the web tools' list, or a SourceBook shared with the pool; kind `local`) and prints its `[S#]`; `_sources` includes it. **P14**: a local item goes ahead of internet candidates only when an alias names it or its score is at least the best internet score; others take their place by score. **P17**: a surrounding code fence is removed before the gate. Step metadata: `contract`, `contract_missing`, `unused`, `not_needed`, `causes`, `tool_calls`, `files_made`; trace: `step_contract`, `contract_check`, `rework_skipped`, `local_source`; result.json `refinement.contract`. The as-built page draws G1–G7 as closed (solid green) with where each wire now is
spec_table.why: LLM proposes, plain code disposes, applied to the step outcome itself: the helper still decides what to do, but whether a step is done, what the answer admits and what gets reworked now follow from recorded evidence. The escape line (NOT NEEDED) keeps a role-wide tool from marking every step of that role partial

spec_table.original: **Equal tool access for the baselines (`--equal-tools on`, default off).** For the five-task benchmark the three architectures must get the same toolbox.
