Checked before the runs: (1) the D32 web grant (a role that asked for web search gets web_search and fetch_url) ran only in the plan runner; (2) the AgentVerse boss_reviewers runner makes no tool calls at all — its solver and critics only write text (AgentVerse vertical-solver-first), so pool and local tools attached to its agents could never be used; (3) plan helpers get 8,192 tokens of reply room per call (D27), flat and boss_reviewers the client default (2,048); flat helpers already call tools with its AutoAgents Action / ActionInput format, including pool and local tools
spec_table.ours: With the flag: (1) `grant_web` applies the D32 rule to flat and boss_reviewers teams; (2) in boss_reviewers each agent with tools may reply with an `Action: <tool>` / `ActionInput: <input>` pair, which runs through `_dispatch` like every other tool call and its result comes back as the next user message (at most `max_turns` = 5 calls, then it is asked once for its answer); any other reply is its answer, exactly as before; the solver, which writes the whole answer, holds every tool and pool item the team was given, the critics their own; (3) flat and boss_reviewers calls get the same 8,192-token reply room. Nothing else changes: no step contract, no checks, no refine turns, no provenance, no plan graph for the baselines. Without the flag both runners are byte-for-byte as before (tests/test_equal_tools.py)
spec_table.why: a comparison is only fair if every architecture can reach the same tools; how each one decides to use them is what is being compared

spec_table.original: **The Action Observer: a mid-run re-plan (`--replan on`, default off).** AutoAgents has an Action Observer in its code: `ActionObserver._think` (autoagents/roles/action_observer.py:30-62) calls `NextAction` (autoagents/actions/steps.py:16-89) after every step; one LLM call reads the task, the roles, the whole history and the unfinished steps, and returns `NextStep` (the next unfinished step, or a new step for an existing role) and `NecessaryInformation` (the facts from the history that step needs). It may not create roles (steps.py:48). In v0.2 this path is dead: it is only reachable through the commented-out block in `Environment.create_roles` (environment.py:128); the live runner (`Group`, group.py) walks the plan in order and never re-plans.
spec_table.ours: Ours runs only when plain code finds a trigger after a wave: a step partial or incomplete for a missing capability, a verify step still FAIL after rework (or with no rework possible), a `MISSING INPUT:` line in a step's output, or a tool or skill a helper with a waiting step holds that the draft never named. No trigger, no call. One call (planner role group, `plan_replan.txt`) sees the task, requirements, the plan with each step's status, the finished outputs (head and tail) with sources and files, what is blocked and why, the tools really held and available, and what is left of the allowance, and returns ONE typed decision with a reason: CONTINUE, REVISE_REMAINING (Box 2 plan format, not-run steps only), ADD_STEP (optional `feeds:`), REASSIGN_STEP, DROP_STEP (names the requirement left unmet) or ADD_ROLE (at most one per run, with a complete role card). Plain code validates: finished steps never change; roles must exist (or be the one added, card complete, team within the envelope's size); new steps depend only on finished or new steps; no cycle; the answer step cannot be dropped and waits for every new step; new capability requests (and a new role's unregistered tools) go through the normal toolbox step (`stock_toolbox(restock=True)`); a dropped requirement goes to Limitations as NOT MET. At most 2 observer calls and 3 added steps per run; an unreadable or invalid reply counts as CONTINUE and is logged. Deviations from AutoAgents: called on triggers, not after every step; decisions are typed and validated by code; it may add one role; it never extracts or rewrites history (steps still see only their inputs). Records: plan.v1.json, plan.v2.json … with a diff; trace `replan_trigger`, `replan_decision`, `replan_validated`, `plan_version`, `requirement_status`; result.json `replan` (calls, accepted, rejected, decisions, steps and roles added, each requirement met / partly / not met and the steps that met it; the answer step counts only when no other step covers the requirement). Smoke-run follow-ups (one live bench5 run before the rerun): a revision may renumber the answer step (old step 4 rewritten as work, the writer moved to 5), so the answer step is found again in the proposed plan (the summariser's step nothing builds on) and only new steps not built on it are added to its depends_on — before, this made a cycle and every such revision was rejected; a tool a role was granted (D32 web tools, D65 verifier tools) is never announced as unavailable nor listed as a contract need; a skill's own script under workspace/skills (recalc.py) is not a missing claimed file
spec_table.why: a plan fixed before the run cannot react when a capability turns out missing or a check keeps failing; the AI proposes the change, code decides whether it is allowed

spec_table.original: Plain-code caps on what a later step sees (D44 `--max-input-chars`, `--max-summary-input-chars`) and on a local tool's output kept only the first N characters
spec_table.ours: **Outputs are never cut before the key result.** `amoeba/interp/shorten.py::shorten` keeps the head AND the tail with `[… N characters omitted …]` marks, and always keeps the lines that carry a final result (count, total, sum, result, answer, largest, an `=` line, a `label: number` line) and the last 20 lines of each program-output block; a single line longer than a quarter of the limit (a printed list) is itself shortened to its head and tail. Used by the plan runner's input assembly (`PlanRunner.cap`, every step input and the summariser's share) and by the local tools' output cap. `plan_step.txt` now asks for results and short excerpts, never whole lists or whole program outputs. Test: the bench5 primes step output (8,087 characters, the 1,229 primes on one line, then `Count: 1229` / `Max Prime: 9973`) now reaches the checker and the writer with both numbers
spec_table.why: in the five-task benchmark the program's own count line was cut away before the checker and the writer, so a correct, executed result was reported as unverified

spec_table.original: A verify step (D34/D61) had only the tools its role was drafted with and saw the checked steps' text and a one-line summary of their tool calls; a PASS was accepted whatever it rested on
spec_table.ours: **Check steps can really check (with `--step-contract on`).** Before a verify step, plain code gives its helpers the tools to re-check what its producers made — calc for numbers, web_search / fetch_url for cited facts, local:Bash / local:Read for code and files (registered through the same local toolbox, so the same sandbox gate `amoeba/localtools/gate.py` screens every call) — and appends to its inputs the raw tool results (up to 8 per step, each shortened by D64) of every step it builds on, directly or through other steps. Its prompt asks it to re-run code or open files and to re-check at least one cited figure, and to name each re-check. Step contract rule: a PASS on steps that produced code, files or cited figures with zero tool calls in the verify step is recorded as an unverified check (`unverified_check`, status partial). Each step_<n>.json keeps `tool_results`; trace `verifier_tools`. Tests: the bench5 primes checker (PASS on reading the code → unverified check; after re-running it → done) and the round-1 weather checker (depends on step 2 only, now sees step 1's forecast)
spec_table.why: in the five-task benchmark and round 1 a checker passed or failed work it had no way to re-check: no file access, no code runner, and no view of the forecast it was meant to check against

spec_table.original: D33 counted a figure as derived only when it followed "=" or appeared in any tool result, and an [unverified] tag always won; a task-given number tagged with an [S#] counted as cited
spec_table.ours: **Provenance fixes.** (1) A number equal, to the precision it is written with, to a calc or local-tool result of the same step (`computed_values`, `equals_computed`) is derived whatever its tag, and plain code removes an `[unverified]` right after it (`strip_unverified`; `unverified_tags_removed` in step_<n>.json). Web results do not count as computed. (2) A number given in the task whose line carries only search / fetched-page source ids (`web_ids`) that do not contain it stays "given" and is listed in `given_with_web_tag`, which earns a refine finding ("write them without a source tag"). `plan_step.txt`: a calc or local result is derived, never [unverified]; a task number needs no tag and never a web [S#]. Tests: bench5 loan (the calc-computed $4,950.30 tagged [unverified]) and diesel ("Fuel Efficiency: 6.5 mpg [S1]")
spec_table.why: in the five-task benchmark Amoeba tagged a twice-computed payment [unverified], and cited a web page for the task's own 6.5 mpg

spec_table.original: A research step took the first dated figure it found, and nothing checked its date
spec_table.ours: **Freshness.** For a task that says today / current / latest / now (`amoeba/interp/freshness.py::time_sensitive`), a step whose helpers hold web tools is asked (FRESH_NOTE) for the most recent official figure with its as-of date, and for one more search for a newer value when the one found is dated. Plain code finds the as-of dates the outputs give for their figures (`as of …`, `Date: …`, `updated …`, `week of …`; a date that is itself the fact, such as a start date, does not count) and, when the newest is more than 3 days before the run, adds "Possibly not the latest (dated …, N days before this run)" to the answer's Limitations (trace `freshness`, summary_check `stale_figure`). Test: bench5 diesel ($6.29 dated September 14, 2026, used on September 28)
spec_table.why: in the five-task benchmark Amoeba's diesel answer used a price a week older than the one the official source had already published, without saying so

spec_table.original: The d24 Planner and Agent Observer saw only the installed tools (calc, echo) and the Plan Observer none; a file format was often requested as a tool; what only the user can supply (brand style, internal data) was settled by assumption; the task-intake check (D52) knew eight verbs and ended a phrase at any dot or comma
spec_table.ours: **Box 2 gaps.** (a) `toolbox_text` lists every tool Box 3 will really have — the installed tools, web_search / fetch_url with --web-tools, the local tools and the local document skills with --local-tools on, and that a tool pool exists (--pool) — and how a role gets each; run_task (and eval_draft with the same flags) passes it to the Planner and both observers (the Plan Observer prompt gains a Tools section). (b) Planner: a document format (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf) or a house style is a SKILL, not a tool. (c) Planner rules and Plan Observer checklist item 9: anything only the user or their company can supply (brand style, internal data, credentials, account access) is an Open Question or a capability request, never an assumption. (d) `quality.py`: deliverable verbs widened (run, convert, email, make, save, write, list, read, compute, compare, find, calculate, report, create, draft, send, summarise, cite, turn, put, show); a phrase ends at sentence punctuation followed by a space, a comma followed by a space, a new line, a bracket or a joining word — not inside an email address, a file name or a decimal
spec_table.why: the planner planned around tools it believed missing, requested formats as tools, and assumed things only the user knows

spec_table.original: A request for a document format went to the one AI pick with the local skill among internet candidates; the picker could choose an outside service (round 1 deck: `presentation-generator` → SlideForge, then refused as side_effect, so the request stayed unfilled)
spec_table.ours: **Tool picking prefers the local document-format skill.** `amoeba/pool/match.py::document_format` reads the format a request names (pptx: pptx, powerpoint, presentation, slide(s), deck; xlsx: xlsx, excel, spreadsheet, workbook; docx: docx, word document; pdf) from its name, standard name, what it does and output. When the local toolbox has a vetted skill for that format (`LocalToolbox.format_skill`), plain code attaches it with no AI pick (`pool_match` records `format_skill`); every other request goes to the picker as before, and an outside service that creates things stays refused (side_effect, D58/D60). Test: the round-1 deck request gets the pptx skill
spec_table.why: the pick is the wrong place to spend a model call when the format decides the answer, and it chose a service we must refuse

spec_table.original: **Harness fixes in our port of the baselines, not changes to their design** (seen in the five-task benchmark): (a) AutoAgents' own prompt teaches a Write File block (`>>>file name` / content / `>>>END`, custom_action.py:41-45, still verbatim in `autoagents_custom_action.txt`), but our local Write tool takes JSON, so every such call was refused as bad input; (b) the flat reader kept the AutoAgents split at every `##`, cutting a finished answer at its first `###` sub-heading; the D62 reader stripped only a well-formed leading `<thought>` block, so a malformed `<thought` let a writer's last tool request become the answer; (c) each architecture's run made its own pool pick, so one lost a code runner by chance; (d) D62 had to be re-checked after D63–D69
spec_table.ours: (a) `file_block_write` (runtime.py) turns such a block, written as local:Write or AutoAgents' 'Write File' by a helper that holds local:Write, into the JSON call (trace `file_block_adapted`); the paper's prompt is unchanged. (b) All three readers: `full_action_input` (moved to runtime.py) is used by the flat runner too, so the ActionInput runs to the end of the reply; `strip_thought` removes every thinking block wherever it stands, malformed openings and orphan closings too, `<think>`/`<thinking>` as well; a boss_reviewers reply that is only a tool request (or empty) is asked once more for the answer (trace `not_an_answer`) and a run whose last answer is still one ends with error `no_answer`. (c) `--picks-file FILE`: `SharedPicks` stores one pick per task and request (under a file lock); every run of the task reuses it when it passes vetting again (trace `pool_pick_reused`); `--picks-only` makes the picks in a pre-pass before the architectures run. (d) Re-checked: the D32 web grant, boss_reviewers tool calls and the 8,192-token reply room hold for flat and boss_reviewers after D63–D69 (test); D63–D67 are Amoeba's own control logic and stay out of the baselines
spec_table.why: a comparison of architectures is only fair when the harness does not lose their work for them

spec_table.original: The sandbox had libreoffice-core only, so `soffice --headless` failed on every file ("source file could not be loaded"): the xlsx skill's scripts/recalc.py always failed, a correct spreadsheet step ended partial ("lacked: scripts/recalc.py"), and no formula ever had a computed value
spec_table.ours: **The office suite works headless.** Cause found with strace: the file is opened, but without the Calc component no filter can load it. `scripts/setup_office.sh` installs libreoffice-calc (no recommends); `amoeba/localtools/office.py::recalc` runs soffice with a fresh profile folder and HOME per call and saves the workbook back with every formula computed; `office_check` proves it on a two-cell workbook (2, 3, =A1*A2 → 6). When the xlsx skill is attached the local toolbox runs the check once (trace `office_check`) and, when it fails, the helper's card says recalc.py will fail. No formula evaluator package was needed. Tests: the two-cell workbook and the bench5 shipment file (Total row → 43, 1,855.81, 79,800) — skipped where Calc is not installed (CI) — and the not-installed path
spec_table.why: spreadsheet steps were marked partial and unverifiable because of the machine, not the team

spec_table.original: Found while redrafting the five-task benchmark (bench5b): `parse_sections` splits a reply on every `##` (AutoAgents `OutputParser.parse_blocks`, system/utils/common.py:33). The loan task's Planner wrote role prompts as JSON strings containing `Output format:\n## Formula`, so the Created Roles List was cut at the first such `##`, no role parsed, and after three rounds the draft failed as "empty plan"
spec_table.ours: **A heading inside a JSON string is not a section break.** `amoeba/task/parsers.py::split_blocks` does not split on a `##` that follows a written `\n` (backslash-n inside a string); a real heading at the start of a line or after `</thought>` still splits. Box 2 is shared by all three architectures, so this changes no comparison. Test: tests/test_parsers.py (the loan reply's shape: three roles survive, the prompt keeps its `## Result`)
spec_table.why: the original split is kept for every other `##`

spec_table.original: A one-off BMV test run (after bench5b) died three times on HTTP 500 "Internal error encountered" from the model service: the client retried only 429/503 and dropped connections, so one 500 ended the run. Each rerun then paid again for work already done: after the first fetched page, every prompt differed from the crashed run's, because a fetched source is labelled with the time it was read ("fetched 2026-09-28T20:56:53") and a page replayed from the web cache got a new time
spec_table.ours: **Crash resilience.** (1) `amoeba/llm/client.py`: HTTP 500, 502 and 504 are retried like 429/503 — the same exponential waits (2, 4, 8 … s, or Retry-After) and the same cap (`--max-rate-retries`), each wait traced as `rate_limited`. (2) A crashed run is resumable: rerun the same task with the same cache folder and namespace and every finished call replays from the cache. `CachedProvider` now stores the time of the live web call with the result (`amoeba/llm/cache.py::stamped`) and `WebTools` shows that time (`amoeba/tools/web.py::now_iso`, `_source(..., at=)`), so a resumed run builds the same prompts and its LLM calls are cache hits. Tests: tests/test_resume_d73.py — 500/502/504 retried with the same waits and cap; a plan run hit by a lasting 500 on call 7 is rerun minutes later and pays for exactly (clean-run calls − 6), with the same answer; fails with the fix off. Limits: local tool calls (Bash, Write) run again on resume (they change the workspace, so they are not cached), and a resumed run whose tools print times or other changing output diverges from that point
spec_table.why: a model-service error costs only the retries, and a crash never pays twice for finished work

spec_table.original: In the BMV test run the check step concluded "Open, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM M–F" and tagged it [S6], the BMV holiday schedule; that text was in S7, IN.gov's Business Owner's Guide (state office hours, not the branch). D33 only checks that a tag names a source the step could see, not that the source says what it is cited for
spec_table.ours: **Citation check by code** (`amoeba/interp/citecheck.py::mislabelled_citations`, plan runner). Every [S#] tag backs the words in front of it (from the previous tag or the line start). In that stretch plain code takes the claims it can test without a model: quoted phrases (≥ 3 words or 12 characters), times of day, and numbers (prices, percentages, counts, date parts) — leaving out list markers, labels (step 3, R2), numbers given in the task, today's date parts and values the step computed. Each must appear in the text the team was really shown for that source (search snippets, the fetched page, a local or pool tool's output — now kept per source, `amoeba/tools/web.py::note_seen`), after normalising case, dashes, a.m./AM, spaces and thousands separators; a number also matches at higher precision in the source ($6.47 vs 6.4709). A miss is a **mislabelled citation**: recorded in the step's artifact (`mislabelled_citations`, with the source that does contain it when one does), trace `mislabelled_citation`, the step becomes partial (reason "mislabelled citation: …"), and the answer's Limitations get "Mislabelled citation: step N cites S6 for '8:00am', which S6 does not contain; it is in S7 (added by plain code)". Plan runner only, like D33 (the baselines have no plain-code step checks). Tests: tests/test_citecheck_d74.py — the BMV checker line (both spellings) flagged on S6 with S7 named; claims that are in their source pass (times, a rounded price, a quote, a date); quotes and numbers; a full plan run → step partial and the Limitations line
spec_table.why: a citation that points at a page which does not say it is caught by code, not left to the model

spec_table.original: In the BMV test run no step was told the date: one team decided it was "Tuesday, May 14, 2024"; another took Monday hours from "general knowledge" when its source left Monday out; the check step preferred a general state office-hours page over a page about the branch
spec_table.ours: **Research rules and the run's clock.** (1) `amoeba/interp/clock.py::run_clock` gives every Box 3 step prompt today's date, weekday and time zone (`--timezone`, an IANA name; default the machine's zone; only the date, not the time of day, so a resumed run replays the same day, D73), trace `run_clock`. The plan runner puts it in its templates (`${today}` in plan_step, plan_summarise, plan_replan, plan_critique); the two baselines keep their papers' prompts verbatim and see it appended to the task text — a fact about the run, like the D62 tool list, given to all three. (2) `plan_step.txt`, general rules (no task-specific wording): prefer the source about the specific thing asked (this branch, this product, this person) over general pages; never infer a specific fact from a general page (an office list, a chain-wide schedule, a category page); if sources disagree say so, name them and prefer the most specific and most recent; if a source lists some days, items or cases and leaves one out, do not fill the gap from general knowledge. Amoeba's own prompt, like D67's freshness note. Tests: tests/test_clock_d75.py — the line (date, weekday, zone; the date where the run is, not UTC); a "today" question has the date in every plan step and summary prompt; flat and boss_reviewers helpers see it on the task text; the rules are in plan_step and no prompt names a task; the CLI flag
spec_table.why: a team never has to guess the date, and a general page is not read as a fact about one place

spec_table.original: In the BMV test run step 1 used all its turns on searches and its "output" was its last search query ('"Hammond" BMV hours "Monday" site:in.gov'); the check step then took one call with 142,000 characters of input (every raw result of the step it checked, plus its own)
spec_table.ours: **Step endings and evidence size.** (1) A helper's last turn offers only Final Output, with "THIS IS YOUR LAST TURN … write your conclusion from what you have found so far, with the [S#] of what supports each fact, and say plainly what you could not confirm"; if it still asks for a tool, the tool is not run and it is asked once more (trace `last_turn_forced`); a second refusal ends the turn with no action. (2) `no_conclusion` (plan runner): an output that is empty, equal to one of the step's tool inputs or unanswered requests, Action/ActionInput syntax, a bare URL, or a lone search string (one short line with search operators or quoted terms and no sentence) fails a `conclusion` check by code — the step is incomplete ("checks failed: conclusion") and can be reworked. (3) A verify step's raw evidence (D65) is now the excerpts that bear on the claims being checked: each result's first line plus every line or 300-character piece holding one of the claims' numbers or times, a quoted phrase, or two words of a line that cites a source, omitted parts marked "[…]"; a result with nothing relevant keeps only its head; at most 20,000 characters in all, with "[… N characters of raw evidence left out: cap 20,000 characters …]". Tool results kept per step for this: up to 6,000 characters each (was 1,500). Tests: tests/test_endings_d76.py — the BMV query-only output has no conclusion, real conclusions do; the last turn offers only Final Output and runs no tool; a plan step that ends on a query fails `conclusion`; excerpts keep the matching lines and drop the rest; the cap and its marker
spec_table.why: a step always ends in a statement that can be checked, and a check step reads the evidence that matters, not everything

spec_table.original: The parking-citation test ("How to pay the P and W universities parking citation?"): the Planner wrote the open question "Which specific universities are P and W?" and settled it with a guess; all three architectures then researched a pair of well-known universities (Purdue + Washington, Purdue + Wisconsin, Purdue + West Virginia); nobody read "P and W" as a dictated "PNW" (Purdue University Northwest, the intended school); the check steps confirmed facts but never questioned what the task was about
spec_table.ours: **Task understanding before planning (Box 1 → Box 2).** (1) `amoeba/task/interpret.py::read_task`: one call (prompt `interpret.txt`, role group planner) lists the task's key entities and terms that could be read more than one way — names, abbreviations, acronyms, likely voice-input errors — each reading with a one-line reason and a confidence (structured: entity, readings[], confidence). (2) Plain code (`decide`): a reading that beats the next by DOMINANCE_GAP = 0.3 or more, or the only one, is the working interpretation; otherwise the subject is ambiguous: with `--interactive` the user gets ONE multiple-choice question (the readings + other) before planning (`ask_one`); without it the top reading is an assumption, and after the run plain code makes the answer open with "I read X as Y; if you meant Z, the answer below may not apply." and lists the other readings under Limitations, adding whatever is missing (`enforce_opening`, trace `assumption_stated`) — in all three architectures. The working interpretation is appended to the task text, so the Planner, both observers and every Box 3 helper read it; the Planner prompt says the subject is not its to settle, and an open question that names an interpreted entity is answered from the interpretation, not the Planner's guess (`route_open_questions`, trace `subject_questions_routed`). (3) `--context user.yaml` (location, organisation, role; other keys ignored): read-only (`amoeba/memory/context.py::load_context`, a MappingProxyType), read only by the interpretation step — the first stub of the Memory box (the full spec's experience memory, archive/experience.py, is a later layer). (4) Plan Observer checklist item 10: does the plan's reading of the task match the recorded working interpretation? run_task `--interpret on` by default; eval_draft `--interpret on|off` (default off, so earlier benchmark drafts are unchanged) and `--context`; a saved draft keeps the interpretation, so every run that reuses it states the same reading. result.json `interpretation`. Tests: tests/test_interpret_d77.py — the decision rule; "P and W" with context organisation Purdue University Northwest → PNW, no question, the planner and every helper see it; no context + --interactive → exactly one multiple-choice question; no context, non-interactive → the answer opens with the stated assumption and Limitations list the alternatives (not duplicated when the team wrote it); an open question about the subject is routed; item 10 is in the Plan Observer prompt
spec_table.why: what the task is about is settled before planning, by the user or by a stated assumption, never by a silent guess

spec_table.original: The BMV dev rerun (docs/eval/dev/REPORT.md §3): S1 printed the branch's ZIP+4 run together ("463243348"); the D74 number check read it as one number, flagged "46324 not in S1" although the ZIP was there, and the step's rework cost one Amoeba run 18 minutes. The number check also split a phone number into three numbers and could round a street number
spec_table.ours: **Identifiers are whole tokens** (`amoeba/interp/citecheck.py::identifiers`, `_identifier_in`). Before the number scan, plain code takes out phone numbers ("(219) 989-2012", "219.989.2012", optional +1), ZIP codes (after a state abbreviation, or written ZIP+4 with a hyphen) and street numbers (a number before a capitalised street name ending in St, Ave, Blvd, Rd, Dr, Ln, Way, Hwy, Pkwy, Ct, Pl…). Each is matched digits-only as a whole token, never rounded or found inside a longer number: a phone with any separators; a 5-digit ZIP alone, as ZIP+4 hyphenated or run together ("463243348" contains 46324); a ZIP+4 only with the same extension; a street number not inside a longer number or written with a thousands separator. A bare 5-digit number in the plain number check also passes when the source has it as the start of a 9-digit ZIP+4. Phase 2 spec §13 row D78. Tests: tests/test_citecheck_d74.py — the BMV line passes against "463243348" (ZIP, street address, ZIP+4); a different extension and a ZIP inside a 10-digit account number are flagged; a phone whose digit groups appear separately is flagged as one phone; a street number is not found inside a longer one
spec_table.why: the citation check no longer flags an address or phone number that is in its source, so a correct step is not reworked

spec_table.original: Phase 2 spec §13: the PNW no-context draft (docs/eval/dev/REPORT.md §2) had only two roles and a writer that verified without tools, and the Plan Observer approved it; the D28 quality gate that would send such a draft back was opt-in and had never been used in a benchmark. Phase 2 adapts Amoeba's recipe on top of Box 2, so Box 2's own floor should be on
spec_table.ours: **The Box 2 quality gate is on by default for Amoeba's plan runner** (`scripts/run_task.py::quality_gate_on`). `--quality-gate on|off|auto`, default `auto`: on for `--topology plan`, off for the baselines (flat, boss_reviewers keep their papers' drafting) and with `--drafts-from` (nothing is drafted); a bare `--quality-gate` still means on, and an explicit choice wins. The gate itself is unchanged (D28: a failed hard draft_quality check sends the draft back within the round cap). `eval_draft.py`, which drafts once for all three architectures in the benchmarks, keeps its opt-in default, so the shared drafts stay shared. This is the only Box 1–3 default Phase 2 changes. Tests: tests/test_quality_gate_d79.py — auto is on for plan only and off with --drafts-from; explicit on/off and the bare flag; main passes the resolved value per topology
spec_table.why: Amoeba's own drafts must pass the hard draft checks before Box 3 runs; the baselines are unchanged

spec_table.original: Phase 2 spec §2: the adaptation loop needs a fixed stream of tasks per family with a shift it must notice, held-out tasks it may test on but never learn from, and a feedback channel that tells it what was missing without handing it the rubric
spec_table.ours: **Box 0, the task stream** (`amoeba/adapt/stream.py`). `tasks/stream_<name>.jsonl`: the Task fields plus `split` (practice / heldout), `phase` (pre / post the family's shift) and `order` (practice only; a held-out task with an order, or any stream task without a rubric, is refused). `tasks/stream_<name>.shifts.yaml`: `feedback` shifts (`after`, `family`, `items`: the post-phase rubrics carry the new items) and `remove_tool` shifts (`tool`). Plain code checks the stream when it is loaded: every post task of the family has each feedback item and no pre task does, no prompt mentions it, a practice task's phase agrees with its order. `Stream.practice()` is the only way the loop gets tasks (stream order; `assert_practice` raises `HeldOutLeak` on a held-out task); `heldout(family, phase)` is for the Experimenter only; `shifts_due` / `disabled_tools` say what is in effect for a practice task. **Feedback channel:** `feedback(rubric_result)` returns only the names of the failed items — no patterns, expected numbers or evidence. **Leakage screen** (`leaks`, used by the Gate): an edit text with an 8-word run of a held-out prompt, a held-out expected number or a held-out task id. **`run_task --disable-tools a,b`** (`disable_tools`): the tools leave the registry (so the envelope and the D68 toolbox text Box 2 sees), the pool (`PoolSetup.disabled`, by id or name) and, for `local:<Name>`, the local tools' allow list; `result.json` gets `disabled_tools` and the trace `tools_disabled` — both only when the flag is used, so a Phase 1 record is unchanged. The milestone stream `tasks/stream_m1*` is committed separately, after it is approved, and is frozen from then on. Tests: tests/test_stream_d80.py — shifts apply from order after+1 and only to their family; held-out tasks never come out of `practice()` and raise when handed to the loop; malformed streams are refused; the feedback record holds item names only; the leakage screen; --disable-tools removes a tool from the registry, envelope, toolbox text, pool and local tools, and a normal run's result.json has no `disabled_tools`
spec_table.why: the loop can be driven by a fixed task stream with shifts, and code guarantees what it may and may not see

spec_table.original: Phase 2 spec §3: the loop adapts a team **recipe** per task family, never a single task's draft; it needs a small typed edit menu (so an edit can be tested, repeated or refused by code) and a validation that keeps a recipe from weakening the checks
spec_table.ours: **The team recipe, the edit menu and validation** (`amoeba/adapt/recipe.py`, thresholds in `amoeba/config/adapt.yaml`). `Recipe{family, version, parent_version, planner_rules: [Rule{id L#, text}], transforms: [Transform{id T#, op, select: Selector, params}], run_options, created_by seed/human/architect, hypothesis_id}`; the seed recipe of every family is empty; `hash()` covers only what it does (rules, transforms, run options), the arm-A cache key. **Edits** (`Edit{op, params}`, parameters validated per op, unknown keys refused; `key()` = op + normalised parameters, hashed, for the repeat check): add/remove_planner_rule, add_verify_step {select}, tighten_done_when {select, clause}, grant/revoke_tool {select, tool}, add_role_rule {select, text}, set_run_option {name, value}; `apply_edit` is pure (version + 1, parent = the old version). **Selector** (matched by code on DraftPlanStep / DraftedRole fields only): kind work/verify/any (an unset kind is work; the answer step is never selected), roles_with_tool, last_work_step, all_roles (the summariser is never a target). **Transforms on the Draft** (`apply_transforms`, used by D82): add_verify_step inserts after each matching step a `kind: verify` step that depends on it (steps renumbered, the answer step also depends on the check), assigned to the team's checker role — one that owns a verify step, else one whose name says it checks, else a new "Checker" (adapt.yaml; D65 hands it the re-check tools at run time), else, in a full team, a role not in the checked step; tighten_done_when appends a clause; grant/revoke_tool; add_role_rule appends to the role card's constraints. Each returns what it changed. **Validation** (`validate_recipe(recipe, envelope, sample_draft)`): V1 every tool named is in the registry/allowlist (or web_search, fetch_url, local:Bash, local:Read), not an outside action by the pool's `side_effect` screen, not a paid endpoint; V2 run options whitelisted and in range (replan, self_refine, collab, max_turns 3–8, check_retry_turns 1–3); V3 ≤ 8 rules, ≤ 8 transforms, texts ≤ 300 characters; V4 a denylist of wording that tells the team to skip checks, citations, the sandbox or the contract (reviewed by hand when it fires); V5 after the transforms on a sample draft, step numbers 1..n, depends_on names existing steps, no cycle, every role named exists, team within max_agents. Tests: tests/test_recipe_d81.py — every edit pure and versioned, typed parameters and the normalised key; V1–V5 each in its own case; an empty (or rules-only) recipe returns the draft byte-identical; transforms change only the selected steps and roles and leave the input draft untouched
spec_table.why: the unit of adaptation is data with a fixed, checkable edit menu

spec_table.original: Phase 2 spec §4: a recipe must act at the three points Phase 1 already has (the Box 2 prompts, the Draft between Box 2 and Box 3, the plan runner's settings), and an empty recipe must change nothing, so that any difference between two arms is the edit
spec_table.ours: **The recipe hook in Boxes 2–3** (`scripts/run_task.py::run_one`, `amoeba/adapt/recipe.py::lessons_text, overlay_run_options, load_recipe`, `amoeba/task/draft.py::draft_team(lessons=…)`). `run_task --recipes DIR` loads the current recipe of `task.family` from a store (`index.json` {family: {current: N}}, `<family>/v<N>.yaml`; the Gate's committed store with history is D88); without the flag, or with no recipe for the family, nothing changes. `--topology plan` only: the baselines never get recipes (CLI error; `run_one` raises). **Box 2:** `d24_create_team.txt`, `d24_review_team.txt` and `d24_review_plan.txt` get a `${lessons}` slot right after `${tools}`, empty by default (the prompts are then byte-identical); with planner rules it holds "# Lessons for this kind of task" and the rules as `- L#: text`, plus, for the Planner, "follow each lesson, or say in Risks and Decisions why it does not apply" and, for the Plan Observer, the check item "every lesson is followed by the plan, or the plan says why not". Box 3 helpers never see the rules themselves. **Box 2 → 3:** after the final draft code applies the transforms in order (`apply_transforms`), records what each changed in `plan.json` `recipe_applied` (trace `recipe_applied`) and keeps Box 2's own draft as `draft.json`, which is what a D45 reuse of that run picks. **Box 3:** run options overlay PlanOptions (replan, self_refine, collab, check_retry_turns) and every helper's Limits.max_turns; a flag given on the command line wins (new flags `--check-retry-turns`, `--max-turns`; `explicit_flags`). **Records:** `result.json` `recipe` {family, version, hash, rules, rules_applied, transforms_applied, run_options, run_options_overridden_by_cli, rules_note} and trace `recipe_loaded`; `recipe`, `recipe_applied` and `draft.json` exist only when a recipe is used. **D45 reuse:** `--drafts-from` plus `--recipes` applies only the transforms and run options; the record says the rules need a fresh draft. Tests: tests/test_recipe_hook_d82.py — an empty recipe leaves every prompt, plan.json and result.json (but the recipe record) unchanged; the lessons reach the Planner and both Observers and the check item the Plan Observer; transforms change only the selected steps and roles (team.yaml and the helpers' role cards carry the new rule); run options overlay the defaults and an explicit CLI flag wins; with a saved draft only transforms and run options apply; baselines refuse a recipe; the store returns the family's current version
spec_table.why: a recipe acts at fixed points, and an empty one is provably a Phase 1 run

spec_table.original: Phase 2 spec §8: before any model may propose an edit, the loop needs a ruler — old recipe against new on tasks the loop never learned from, with everything but the edit held fixed, and cheap enough to run per hypothesis
spec_table.ours: **Box 7, the Experimenter** (`amoeba/adapt/experimenter.py`, `scripts/run_experiment.py`; no model call of its own). `experiment(recipe_A, edit, hypothesis_id, stream, runner, root, repeats=3)`: recipe B = `apply_edit(recipe_A, edit)`; for each held-out task of the family (post first, then pre for retention) and each repeat k: arm A drafts afresh with recipe A's rules (seed k) and runs; for a **transform or run-option edit** arm B runs recipe B on arm A's saved draft (`--drafts-from` that run folder, D45 — the arms differ only by the edit), for a **planner-rule edit** arm B drafts with its own rules (seed k; draft variance is part of the noise); same seed, tools, model, time zone and limits; separate LLM cache namespaces per arm and run (a crashed run resumes, the arms never replay each other). **Arm-A cache** (`ArmACache`): `<root>/armA/<recipe hash>/<task>.k<k>.s<seed>/` plus `index.jsonl`, keyed by the recipe's content hash — a later hypothesis against the same version runs arm B only; `calibrate()` (A vs A′, A′ with seeds k + 1000, held-out post slice) fills it. **Pairs** (`Pair`): task, phase, k, seed, score_A/B (D30 rubric fraction), tokens_A/B, honesty_A/B (`honesty_flags`: hallucinated citations + Σ mislabelled citations + Σ claimed files missing + unverified checks + 1 if error), refusals_A/B (local sandbox and pool side-effect refusals), run folders. Written to `<root>/experiments/<id>/{experiment.json, pairs.jsonl, recipes_B/, runs/B/…}`. **Runners:** `SubprocessRunner` (one `python -m scripts.run_task` per job, 8 at once; a run folder with a finished result is reused — D73 resume; a model-service or cache crash is re-run once), `InProcessRunner` (tests). `amoeba/config/adapt.yaml experiment`: repeats 3, parallel 8, the run_task flags of every run, and `option_defaults` (replan on, self_refine on-issues, collab critique) passed as the new `run_task --option-defaults`, which sets them like a default so a recipe's run option still wins (an explicit flag would override it, D82). The family's held-out tasks get a `remove_tool` shift's tool disabled on the post slice. Tests: tests/test_experimenter_d83.py — a transform edit runs B on A's saved draft (no planner call in B, same Box 2 draft, only the edit differs, same seeds); a planner-rule edit drafts in both arms with only B seeing the lessons; the calibration fills the cache and a second hypothesis runs arm B only; honesty flags; the subprocess command
spec_table.why: old against new is measured with everything but the edit held fixed, at half the cost after the first hypothesis

4. Provide a concise execution plan: a numbered sequence of steps that logically reaches the goal, listing the involved roles, expected output per step, and required input for the next step. End with the language expert synthesis step.

Here is an example JSON blob for a role:
{{
    "name": "ROLE NAME",
    "description": "ROLE DESCRIPTONS",
    "tools": ["ROLE TOOL"],

boxes.title: Scoring (after Box 3)
boxes.sentence: Compares the team's answer with the known answer; a job with no single right answer is scored against its rubric instead.
what: After the run, the team's answer is compared with the known answer.
Both are lower-cased, runs of spaces are squeezed to one, and trailing full stops are dropped.

boxes.title: Task interpretation (D77)
boxes.sentence: Before the Planner drafts, an AI lists what the task's names and terms could mean; plain code takes a clear winner, asks the user one question, or makes the answer state its assumption.
what: One call reads the task (and the read-only user context from --context: location, organisation, role) and lists the key entities and terms that could be read more than one way — names, abbreviations, acronyms, likely voice-input errors such as "P and W" for "PNW" — each reading with a one-line reason and a confidence.

Plain code: a reading whose confidence beats the next by 0.3 or more (DOMINANCE_GAP) (or the only one) is the working interpretation. Otherwise, with --interactive, the user gets one multiple-choice question (the readings + other); without it the top reading is an assumption.

The working interpretation is added to the task text, so the Planner, both checkers and every helper in all three runners read it; an open question the Planner writes about one of these names is answered from it, not by its guess.
After the run, when the reading was assumed, plain code makes the answer open with "I read X as Y; if you meant Z, …" and lists the other readings under Limitations, adding whatever is missing.
boxes.proposes: The entities, their readings, a reason and a confidence for each.
boxes.disposes: Plain code decides whether a reading is clear, whether to ask, and checks the answer's opening line.

boxes.sentence: Throws out broken or nameless helper entries, records tools we lack instead of dropping them, flags the summariser, and drops steps that name nobody.

Matches each step's names to helpers (exact first, then by part of the name) and drops steps that match nobody; no steps left means drafting failed.

Measures the draft: every requirement covered, dependencies valid, helpers fully described, one summariser, a checking step done by a helper that did not produce what it checks, and task coverage: every number in the task and every deliverable verb (deliver, estimate, assess, prototype, test, gather, build, plan, and since D68 run, convert, email, make, save, write, list, read, compute, compare and more) must reach a requirement or a given; a phrase ends at sentence punctuation, not inside an email address or a decimal.
With the quality gate on by default, a draft failing a must-have check goes back to the planner for one more round with the failed checks listed, within the round cap.

boxes.title: Check the step
boxes.sentence: Checks each step's output against its requirements, contract, and provenance; reads verdicts, gaps, and citation accuracy.
what: Checks what the planner said the step produces: the table:, list:, code: or memo: markers in its output line (keywords only when there are none), and a real use of its inputs.
A failed check gets one retry with the reasons and two turns of its own; otherwise the step is incomplete.

A step the planner marked kind: verify must answer PASS or FAIL; a FAIL sends each step it checked back once, then it checks again. Steps that already used the old output are marked stale (--rerun-stale redoes them once).
BLOCKED lines make a producer step partial, with the missing capability listed; the answer step is never scanned for them.

Step contract (D61, --step-contract on): before the step, plain code lists each helper's unfilled requests and the items attached to it; after it, every tool call is on record (who, which tool, ok). A lacked capability with no BLOCKED or NOT NEEDED line, or an attached item never used successfully, earns one refine turn and then makes the step partial (not declared / attached unused).

A verify step also sees each checked step's sources, tool calls, figure counts, files, and citation labels (D61, D74). A producer whose only problem is a missing capability is not sent back (rework_skipped).

D65: a verify step also gets the tools to re-check (calc, web search and fetch, local run and read, through the same sandbox gate) and the raw tool results of every step it builds on; a PASS with no re-checking tool call on code, files or cited figures is an unverified check and makes it partial. Evidence is capped at 20,000 characters and excerpts are limited to 240 characters.

boxes.title: Action Observer (re-plan)
boxes.sentence: With --replan on, after a wave where something went wrong or changed, an AI may re-plan the steps that have not run; plain code checks the change before it takes effect.
what: Plain code looks for a trigger after each wave: a step that lacked a capability, a verify step still failing, a step reporting a missing input, a tool the plan did not know about, or a missing answer step. No trigger, no call.

One planner call sees the task, the plan with each step's status, what the finished steps produced, what is blocked, the tools really available, the budget left, and the final answer step, returning one decision: CONTINUE, REVISE_REMAINING, ADD_STEP, REASSIGN_STEP, DROP_STEP or ADD_ROLE.

Code rejects any change to a finished step, unknown roles or tools, an incomplete new role card, a team too large, a loop, or a new step that depends on a step that has not run. New capability requests go through the normal toolbox step; a dropped requirement is listed as not met.
At most 2 re-plans and 3 added steps per run; an unreadable or invalid reply counts as CONTINUE. Each accepted plan is saved as plan.v2.json, plan.v3.json … with the change.
boxes.proposes: One typed decision and its reason.
boxes.disposes: Plain code decides when to call, validates the decision, applies it and records every version.

boxes.sentence_tpl: With --replan on, after a wave where something went wrong or changed, an AI may re-plan the steps that have not run; plain code checks the change before it takes effect.
what_tpl: Plain code looks for a trigger after each wave: a step that lacked a capability, a verify step still failing, a step reporting a missing input, a tool the plan did not know about, or a missing answer step. No trigger, no call.

One planner call sees the task, the plan with each step's status, what the finished steps produced, what is blocked, the tools really available, the budget left, and the final answer step, returning one decision: CONTINUE, REVISE_REMAINING, ADD_STEP, REASSIGN_STEP, DROP_STEP or ADD_ROLE.

Code rejects any change to a finished step, unknown roles or tools, an incomplete new role card, a team too large, a loop, or a new step that depends on a step that has not run. New capability requests go through the normal toolbox step; a dropped requirement is listed as not met.

At most {PlanOptions.max_replans} re-plans and {PlanOptions.max_added_steps} added steps per run; an unreadable or invalid reply counts as CONTINUE. Each accepted plan is saved as plan.v2.json, plan.v3.json … with the change.

Pool tools (D56) are remote MCP servers registered as pool:<name> for the helper that asked; they run here too, with the same caps, [S#] source ids and error lines.

boxes.title: Stock the toolbox
boxes.sentence: Before the team starts, tries to fill each tool or skill the team asked for from the pool; one AI pick per request, everything else plain code.
what: Match: the cached pool entries, tools and skills alike (the requested kind is only the planner's guess; the kind asked and the kind picked are logged), are ranked by the words they share with the request (its standard name and aliases, name, what it does, input and output); the best 5 (pool.yaml) are kept. None above zero: unfilled, no AI call.

Vet first (D60): the candidates are checked before the pick and the AI is shown only the best 5 that pass (up to 50 matches are checked); if none pass, the request is unfilled (all_refused) with no AI call.

Pick: one short AI call shows the request and those candidates and must answer exactly one listed id or NONE; any other reply counts as NONE. It gets 6,000 tokens of room, and once more with twice that when the reply is cut off.

Vet: a tool must be read-only (nothing in its name or description that sends, posts, pays or deletes, or creates, updates, uploads, edits or writes anything in an outside service, D60) and not a pay-per-call host; it needs an HTTPS remote, a source repository, a pinned version, no key or its key in the environment, and an unchanged description (also re-checked against the server's tools/list at every connection); a skill must be instruction-only and at most 5,000 characters. At most 3 items per helper and 8 per run (pool.yaml).
Attach: a tool becomes pool:<name> for the asking helper only; a skill's text goes on that helper's card. All pool text is shown inside marked data blocks, and the 'unavailable' line goes away.
Every request's outcome and reason code is written to capability_requests.json and result.json; without a pool cache the run logs pool_unavailable and goes on as before.

With --local-tools on (D59) the local toolbox's items are candidates too — ahead of the pool's only when an alias names them or they match at least as well (D61) — and a skill with scripts is no longer refused: it is copied into the run's workspace.
What became of each request (filled or not) is handed to the plan runner for the step contract (D61).
D69: a request that names a document format (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf) gets the vetted local skill for it, chosen by plain code with no AI pick; an outside service that creates things stays refused.
D70: with --picks-file every run of a task reuses the task's first pick for a request (all three architectures), when it passes vetting again; --picks-only makes the picks in a pre-pass.

boxes.title: Local toolbox (sandboxed)
boxes.sentence: With --local-tools on, the team may borrow Claude Code's own tools and skills through `claude mcp serve`, inside a workspace folder of the run.
what: Starts `claude mcp serve` once per run over stdio (MCP Python SDK), lists its tools and closes it at the end; only Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep are allowed, every other listed tool is refused and logged once. They become local:<Name> tools of the run.

Needs AMOEBA_SANDBOX=1. Every path must resolve inside runs/<id>/workspace/ (else outside_workspace); a Bash command runs from there, network commands are refused (network_command) and destructive or escaping ones too (unsafe_command).
Limits (localtools.yaml): 60 s per call, 8,000 characters of output, 20 calls per step and 60 per run; a trace line for every call and every refusal.

Skills are listed only from the kept anthropics/skills clone (D60: not the user's ~/.claude/skills); an attached skill's folder is copied to workspace/skills/<name>/ and its SKILL.md (frontmatter and first 5,000 characters) goes on the helper's card.
Aliases (code runner → local:Bash, spreadsheet → the xlsx skill …) put local items first; any other local item goes first only if it matches at least as well as the best internet one (D61).
A successful call's result gets a source id [S#] in the run's one source list (D61); a command written inside a code fence runs without the fence.

A step that says it saved a file the workspace does not hold ends incomplete (claimed_file_missing); result.json lists files_created, local_tool_calls, local_refusals and skills_attached, and the workspace is copied to artifacts/files/.

D71: LibreOffice Calc headless (scripts/setup_office.sh) recalculates spreadsheet formulas with a fresh profile and HOME; when the xlsx skill is attached, plain code checks once that a two-cell workbook comes back with its value, and if not the helper's card says recalc.py will fail.
boxes.proposes: A helper's tool call (name and input); the picker's choice of a local item.
boxes.disposes: Plain code allows the tool, checks every path and command, caps calls and output, and checks claimed files.

boxes.title: AI connection
boxes.sentence: The connection to any AI service that speaks the OpenAI format; it reports what each reply cost in tokens.
what: Sends the messages to the AI service and returns the reply with its token counts.

Waits out rate limits (HTTP 429/503: up to 5 retries, Retry-After honoured, each wait logged), dropped connections and timeouts too; an error still there after that ends the run with error 'api: …' and its records are still written. boxes.title: Team recipe, edit menu and hook (D81–D82)
boxes.sentence: Per kind of task, a small piece of data says what to tell the Planner, how code reshapes the drafted plan and which run settings to use; one typed edit makes the next version.
what: A recipe holds planner rules (lessons shown in Box 2), transforms (applied by code to the final draft) and run options (whitelisted plan-runner settings). Every kind starts from an empty recipe, and an empty recipe changes nothing.

The edit menu: add or remove a planner rule, add a check step after selected steps, add a clause to selected steps' done-when, grant or revoke a tool on selected roles, add a rule to selected roles' cards, set one run option. Each edit is a pure function that makes version N+1 with parent N.

Validation by plain code (V1–V5): tools are in the registry and not outside actions; run options are whitelisted and in range; the number of rules and transforms and the length of each text are capped (amoeba/config/adapt.yaml); no wording that tells the team to skip checks, citations or the sandbox; and the step graph still passes the plan checks after the transforms.

The hook (D82): run_task --recipes DIR loads the family's current recipe (plan runner only; the baselines never get one). Its rules fill the lessons slot of the Planner's and both checkers' prompts, with one more check item for the plan checker; code applies its transforms to the final draft (draft.json keeps Box 2's own draft) and records what each changed; its run options overlay the run settings unless the command line set them. With a reused draft only transforms and run options apply.

boxes.title: 7 · Experimenter (D83)
boxes.sentence: Runs the old recipe against the old recipe plus one edit on the kind's held-out tasks, three times each, with the same seed, tools and model, and returns the score pairs.
what: For each held-out task (after-shift tasks first, then before-shift ones for the retention check) and each repeat, arm A drafts afresh with the old recipe and runs it.

For a transform or run-option edit, arm B reuses arm A's saved draft, so the only difference between the arms is the edit; for a planner-rule edit, arm B drafts with its own rules and draft variance is part of the noise.

Arm A runs are cached per recipe version (by the recipe's hash), so a later hypothesis against the same version runs arm B only; the noise-floor calibration (A against A' with other seeds) fills that cache.

Each pair records both scores, tokens, honesty flags (made-up or mislabelled citations, claimed files missing, checks that re-checked nothing, an error) and refusals. Runs go out as run_task processes, 8 at once; a finished run is never redone, and a model-service crash is re-run once.

boxes.disposes: Plain code builds both arms, runs them and writes the pairs.

boxes.sentence_tpl: Runs the old recipe against the old recipe plus one edit on the kind's held-out tasks, three times each, with the same seed, tools and model, and returns the score pairs.
what_tpl: For each held-out task (after-shift tasks first, then before-shift ones for the retention check) and each repeat, arm A drafts afresh with the old recipe and runs it.

For a transform or run-option edit, arm B reuses arm A's saved draft, so the only difference between the arms is the edit; for a planner-rule edit, arm B drafts with its own rules and draft variance is part of the noise.

Arm A runs are cached per recipe version (by the recipe's hash), so a later hypothesis against the same version runs arm B only; the noise-floor calibration (A against A' with other seeds) fills that cache.

Each pair records both scores, tokens, honesty flags (made-up or mislabelled citations, claimed files missing, checks that re-checked nothing, an error) and refusals. Runs go out as run_task processes, 8 at once; a finished run is never redone, and a model-service crash is re-run once.

glossary: helper
One AI worker in a team, with its own name, instructions and allowed tools.
team shape (topology)
How helpers are connected; fixed when a run starts, never chosen by an AI.
step by step (flat)
The plan's steps run in order; each step's helpers take turns until they give a final answer.
one writer with reviewers (boss + reviewers)
One helper writes the answer, the others review it, the writer revises on objections.
draft
The planner's proposed helpers and step plan for one round.
round
One planner reply plus one reply from each checker.
turn
One reply from each helper of a step.
consensus
Both checkers wrote 'No Suggestions' in the same round.
section
A '## Heading' part of an AI reply that plain code cuts out and reads.
guard
A plain-code check that rejects, corrects or caps what an AI produced (shield icon).
envelope
The fixed rules a team must satisfy: allowed tools per role and the team-size limit.
trace
The log file with one line per AI call, tool call, helper turn and run.
token
The unit AI services count text in; recorded per call, never enforced in Phase 1.
sample run
One practice job run with the offline stand-in AI when this page was built.
stand-in AI
A scripted fake AI used offline; it is not a real model.
deviation
A deliberate difference from the original AutoAgents / AgentVerse code, marked in the source.

gaps.title: Capability record → step status
gaps.missing: Which requests each helper asked for and did not get (capability_requests.json, missing_tools) never reaches the status check: a step is 'done' unless the helper itself wrote BLOCKED.
evidence: r1-route, all rounds: distances from memory in a 'done' step with no routing tool
r1-code-run, round 2b: 'done' without the code being run
gaps.direction: A step whose helper has an unfilled request cannot be 'done' without saying what it did instead.
gaps.fix: D61: before the step plain code lists each helper's unfilled requests (step contract, shown on its prompt); after it, one that is neither BLOCKED nor NOT NEEDED earns one refine turn, then makes the step partial ("not declared by the helper").

gaps.title: Tool-call trace → step status
gaps.missing: Whether the helper called the tool or skill attached for its request is logged (execute_tool, local_call) but never read when the step is judged.
evidence: r1-deck, round 2: pool slide tool attached, 0 calls, step 'done'
r1-deck, round 3: pptx skill + local tools attached, 0 calls, step 'done'
gaps.direction: An attached item that was never called is recorded on the step, and the helper must say why.
gaps.fix: D61: every tool call of the step is recorded (who, tool, ok); an attached item with no successful call and no BLOCKED / NOT NEEDED line earns one refine turn, then makes the step partial ("attached unused").

gaps.title: Capability record → Limitations
gaps.missing: Limitations are built only from the BLOCKED marks helpers wrote; the run's unfilled requests are never compared with the answer.
evidence: r1-fx-email, all 4 rounds: the missing email sender is never named
r1-route: the missing routing tool is never named; r1-weather 2b: missing current conditions not named
gaps.direction: Every unfilled capability request appears in Limitations, whatever the helpers wrote.
gaps.fix: D61: Limitations also get every undeclared missing capability and every attached item left unused (NOT USED lines), matched by canonical name.

gaps.title: Checked step's sources → verifier
gaps.missing: A verify step sees only its declared inputs, not the tool results behind the step it checks.
evidence: r1-weather, round 2: a real, cited forecast fetched in step 1; the verifier (depends on step 2 only) wrote BLOCKED 'Step 1 output' and the answer said 'failed verification'
gaps.direction: A verifier also receives the sources of the steps it checks.
gaps.fix: D61: a verify step's inputs carry, per checked step, its sources, tool calls (ok or failed), figure counts, files made and what it lacked or left unused.

gaps.title: Produced work → answer check
gaps.missing: Figures and files produced upstream (figure ledger, files_created) are recorded but never checked against the final answer; after a FAIL the summariser writes a status memo instead.
evidence: r1-xlsx, rounds 1–2b: lane totals, 79,800 and 1,855.81 computed in step 1, absent from every answer
gaps.direction: The answer carries every usable result produced upstream, next to what is missing.
gaps.fix: D61: the answer step is told which files each step made; files and source-cited figures the answer leaves out earn one refine turn, and files still unnamed are listed by plain code.

gaps.title: Failure cause → rework
gaps.missing: On a FAIL verdict every checked producer is re-run, whatever the cause; a missing capability does not change between attempts.
evidence: rework in 6 of 10 runs in round 2 and again in 2b; none changed a blocked step (r1-full-chain: 3 reworks, 2 stale)
gaps.direction: Skip rework when the producer's only problem is a capability it does not have.
gaps.fix: D61: each step records its causes; a producer whose only cause is a missing capability is not reworked (rework_skipped).

gaps.title: Local tool result → source list
gaps.missing: A local tool's output gets no source id, so provenance cannot count a figure taken from it as cited.
evidence: r1-code-run, round 3: the executed F50 = 12586269025 cited as '[S1]', counted as a made-up citation
gaps.direction: Give each local result a source id ('local run'), shared with the run's [S#] list.
gaps.fix: D61: a successful local call gets an [S#] in the run's one source list (kind local), and the step's sources include it.
